# clanker v1 scope and build approach **Current POC delivery override — 4 October 2026:** use the owner's MacBook as the host, kept running in clamshell mode with Amphetamine. Sahan and Nishank join the existing Slack workspace and use channel mentions of `@clanker`. Cloud hosting, VM pools and laptop-independent availability are deferred for this POC. [POC_SCOPE.md](POC_SCOPE.md) records the local setup and remaining reviewer checks; the hosted design below remains the broader v1 roadmap. ## State **clanker v1 is a hosted Hermes-based Slack assistant for general browser tasks and access management. Reuse Hermes first; focus clanker-specific work on routing and authorization, and add code only for demonstrated gaps.** The repository contains this scope, a verification strategy and source review, plus a pinned stock Hermes local baseline and clanker Slack setup files. The local CLI starts, 47 targeted upstream routing/session tests pass, and real Slack owner commands work in a DM and the test channel; see [LOCAL_BASELINE.md](verification/LOCAL_BASELINE.md). The full Slack/browser E2E, deployed reviewer experience, and v1 acceptance remain open. Upstream documentation and synthetic tests establish narrower capabilities, not that our chosen deployment has passed its requirements. **Selected browser architecture:** each assigned worker VM runs Hermes and local Chromium, controlled through Hermes's existing Browser Use driver. This is the selected v1 design; the VM pool, browser workflow, and persistence across VM replacement still require implementation and verification. **Selected access interface:** a hosted clanker vault web app uses Sign in with Slack to collect and manage saved access. Reuse Hermes's vault implementation and UI/API components behind clanker's authenticated owner and task checks. This integration is selected, not implemented or verified. The assignment permits third-party components and prioritizes a smooth working experience over code volume. A successful v1 may consist mostly of configuration, deployment, integration fixes, and verification. There is no requirement to build a new agent harness, Slack connector, browser engine, vault, or TOTP algorithm. Slack is the v1 conversation interface, with the hosted vault web app for secure access collection and management. The user reported that Sahan approved Slack identity replacing the assignment's Google-only chatbot sign-in requirement. Sahan and Nishank enter through the demo workspace invitation/entry link and use clanker without local setup or their own model-provider accounts. Inference is owner-funded. The assignment's core is browser tasks and secure access management. Private DMs, shared channel context, and protection between reviewers are additional v1 behavior requested by the user. A general self-service SaaS platform is not a prerequisite. ### Preferred inference setup: owner's ChatGPT account Prefer using the owner's existing ChatGPT subscription through Hermes's ChatGPT/Codex OAuth provider for the cloud baseline, to avoid purchasing separate API credits for eligible model usage. Reviewers still use Slack without their own model-provider accounts. This is the preferred setup to evaluate, not a verified funding arrangement. [Hermes documents](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers) device-code authorization, which lets the owner approve login in their browser while Hermes runs and stores its authentication on the cloud host. [OpenAI documents](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001542-using-your-chatgpt-plan-in-other-apps-and-sites) eligible plan usage in supported integrations; Hermes's exact account eligibility and quota accounting remain unverified for this deployment. Before relying on this route, establish that the intended owner-funded reviewer usage is supported, run a small inference request, and inspect the resulting usage and billing. Verify authentication refresh and persistence across a cloud restart with the owner's laptop out of the execution path. Subscription-funded inference does not establish coverage for hosting or separately billed browser/tool services. Record those costs separately. Any alternative paid inference setup remains a separate decision if the preferred route cannot meet the requirements. ## Reuse from Hermes Pin the Hermes version and required integrations, configure them, and verify their behavior in the deployed Slack experience. | Capability | Starting point | What clanker must establish | | --- | --- | --- | | Agent harness | Hermes's agent loop, tools, skills, and session machinery | General tasks work with the selected model and enabled tools. | | Slack interface | Hermes's existing Slack adapter and gateway | App configuration, authenticated admission, correct conversation routing, and replies. | | Browser automation | Local Chromium inside the assigned worker VM, controlled by Hermes's existing Browser Use driver (`browser_exec`) | Background browser work, uploads/downloads, secure login/handoff, scoped browser persistence, and saved-access reuse across worker replacement. | | Credentials and 2FA | Hermes's credential vault, Desktop vault form/API components, protected browser filling, TOTP support, and access-management controls | The hosted clanker vault web app authenticates with Slack and enforces owner/task/site access before saving or using credentials. Reviewers can securely provide, reuse, and remove access. Resolve the TOTP choice below. | | Profiles and conversations | Existing profile routing, DM/channel/thread sessions, memory, and persistence | The selected configuration enforces the intended tenant, owner, and audience boundaries across turns and restarts. | Start from the documented [browser integration](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/browser/), [credential vault](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/credential-vault/), [profile routing](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/multi-profile-gateways/#routing-shared-bot-chats-to-profiles-profile_routes), and [session behavior](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/sessions/#shared-vs-isolated-group-sessions). Native vault UI/API components cover CLI/Desktop use; the selected hosted web app adds the Slack identity and access-request authorization boundary. The complete collection, reuse, and revocation flow still needs validation. ## Architecture and routing contract **Use a shared Slack gateway and a pool of isolated Hermes worker VMs.** The gateway binds authenticated tenant, sender, and conversation audience to an authorized profile before queueing the task. The scheduler assigns a ready VM to that private or shared context; the VM pool manager maintains clean warm spares, adds capacity within limits, and removes excess idle capacity. Each worker runs Hermes, its Browser Use driver, and local Chromium inside the same VM. Profiles and permitted browser/file state persist beyond the worker's lifetime. The hosting provider, pool sizes, idle timeout, and storage implementation remain open choices. ```mermaid flowchart TD Slack["Slack workspaces
Private DMs and shared channels/threads"] <--> Gateway["Hermes Slack gateway"] Gateway --> Routing["Authenticated tenant, sender, and audience
Bind authorized profile and task"] Routing --> Queue["Durable task queue + scheduler
Fair dispatch, leases, bounded retries"] Queue -->|Assign task| Worker["Assigned worker VM
Hermes + Browser Use driver + local Chromium
One authorized private or shared context"] Queue -->|Pending demand| Pool["VM pool manager / autoscaler
Ready-spare target, VM limits, idle timeout"] Pool -->|Lifecycle calls| Provider["VM provider API"] Provider -->|Provision or stop| Worker Worker -->|Capacity and health| Pool Worker <--> Access["Enforced resource access
Only the current context's authorized state"] Access <--> State["Durable profile home, browser state, and files
Separate task and delivery records"] Gateway -->|Private access link| VaultUI["Hosted clanker vault web app"] VaultUI <--> Auth["Sign in with Slack
OIDC identity + server session"] Auth -->|Verified workspace and user| Trusted["Trusted credential handler
Owner, task, site, and action checks"] VaultUI -->|Secure credential submission| Trusted Trusted <--> Vault["Protected durable Hermes vault
Keys inaccessible to agent code"] Access -->|Authorized credential operation| Trusted Trusted -->|Resume after durable save| Queue Worker -->|Persist result| Delivery["Result delivery + owner-bound approval enforcement"] Delivery --> Gateway ``` These boxes describe responsibilities, not mandatory separate services. Reuse Hermes's Slack adapter, agent runtime, browser driver, vault, and session machinery. Routing checks may use existing configuration, supported extension points, or a small clanker integration. The scheduler and VM pool manager can share a backend service. The remote worker-to-gateway handoff must bind and durably record results before releasing a worker; reuse existing Slack delivery where it fits. Run Hermes in its upstream runtime; TypeScript remains the preference for clanker-owned integration code where appropriate. ### Selected browser stack: local Chromium + Browser Use Use the existing [Browser Use driver](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/browser/#browser-use-mode-default) with local Chromium. Hermes remains the agent making decisions; Browser Use supplies browser control through `browser_exec`. A hosted browser service is not part of the selected v1 baseline. Make local selection explicit instead of relying on credential autodetection: ```yaml browser: cloud_provider: local backend: browser-use ``` Build the worker image with pinned, compatible versions of Hermes, the Browser Use CLI, `agent-browser`, Chromium, and the required Linux dependencies. The pinned Hermes release installs/discovers the Browser Use CLI separately; pinning Hermes alone does not pin that driver. Complete installation during image construction so assigned tasks do not depend on first-use downloads. Keep **Hermes itself, the Python executed by `browser_exec`, and Chromium inside the assigned VM**. Running only the browser there would leave driver code executing on the shared host. Expose only the current context's authorized profile, browser state, and files; a shared channel worker must not receive a participant's private account state. Persist the authorized profile state, including `state.db` conversation and tool history, plus the dedicated browser profile and required workspace files/artifacts. Keep the protected vault and its decryption keys outside agent-accessible profile mounts, as specified below. Clanker's task record references the Hermes profile and session rather than duplicating chat history. Default local Chromium sessions are temporary, so configure and verify a persistent browser profile; a dedicated local Chromium instance connected through CDP is an existing integration option. The exact persistence mechanism remains to be validated. Restoring conversation history and cookies does not by itself restore a live page, unfinished form, or in-flight action. Before accepting this stack, exercise secure credential filling and human login/handoff, saved-login reuse in a fresh browser, saved-session reuse separately, download/inspection or transformation/upload, owner/audience separation, revocation, and recovery after worker replacement. These are pending acceptance checks, not capabilities already verified in clanker's local baseline. ### Selected access flow: hosted vault + Sign in with Slack Send the owner a private link to an expiring access request. The hosted clanker vault web app authenticates with Slack OpenID Connect and can reuse a valid server session for later visits. Validate the token signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and nonce, and validate OAuth state on the redirect. Match the verified Slack `team_id` and `user_id` to the request's tenant and owner; the server also binds the task, site origin, and permitted action. Reject a mismatched identity, expired request, or replay, and consume the request once on successful submission. Neither an email address, URL parameter, nor possession of the link grants access. This Sign in with Slack flow is separate from the Slack bot installation OAuth flow. Reuse Hermes's vault storage, validation, browser-fill/TOTP primitives, and existing Desktop form/API components where suitable. Clanker supplies the hosted page, authenticated session, request authorization, and task-resumption integration; exposing the general Hermes dashboard or accepting a client-selected profile is not that boundary. The existing optional setup-key field is reusable capability, not a decision to enable automatic TOTP; the product choice below remains unresolved. Submit secrets directly from the secure form to a trusted credential handler. Passwords and setup keys must bypass Slack, model inputs, task queue payloads, and application logs. The handler selects authorized storage from trusted identity, persists it durably, and returns only a handle and safe metadata. Keep the handler and decryption keys in an execution boundary inaccessible to arbitrary agent code; a context-local profile switch or a vault key beside agent-readable files does not enforce this. Authorized browser filling uses the protected path without returning the secret to the model. The exact boundary and Hermes integration require implementation and verification. Persist `waiting_for_input` and the access request independently of the worker VM. After a successful durable save, atomically consume the request and record the task's readiness for resumption, with idempotent dispatch so retries cannot lose or duplicate the resume transition. Requeue the original task with the credential handle, not the secret; an active worker need not remain online while the owner fills the form. Verify that saving during worker replacement resumes the correct task and that removing access prevents further affected credential use and saved-session reuse. | Routing decision | Required behavior | | --- | --- | | Tenant | Derive workspace/installation identity from authenticated Slack events. Include it in user, conversation, and resource routing. Reject unknown or unauthorized requesters instead of falling into a privileged default. | | Conversation and audience | A 1:1 DM loads that user's private context. A channel/thread loads context authorized for that channel's audience. Workspace membership alone does not reveal private-channel history. | | Requester and resource owner | Keep the sender, account/resource owner, and conversation audience distinct. Validate ownership before using credentials, browsers, files, history, or controls. Another participant's follow-up conveys no authority over someone else's private work. | | Context and tools | Scope memory, session recall, learned skills, files, artifacts, browser state, and credentials to the current authorized context. Prompt instructions and model-supplied owner IDs cannot grant access. | | Result destination | Return private account results privately. Sharing requires the owner's approval of the specific content and audience. Shared output grants no access to its source account or private files. | Session separation and profile routing are useful controls, but must be tested together with tools and persistence. Shared-profile memory or session recall must not expose DM content in a channel. Model-generated code must not have unrestricted access to other owners' files, the shared history store, or platform administrator credentials. Use supported scoped tools and isolated execution where needed; disable or adapt a tool whose access cannot be constrained. Keep retained history, recovery state, browser access, and artifacts durable across restarts, with their owner/audience associations intact. Use existing persistence when it meets these needs. The VM execution boundary and local browser stack above are selected; the cloud vendor, storage technology, and exact profile/session mapping remain implementation choices. For v1 delivery, the reviewers use one demo workspace. Routing must still carry tenant identity and be checked against another tenant identity without requiring a public onboarding or provisioning product. ### Example: collaboration involving a private account Sahan and Nishank discuss a report in a shared thread. Both contributions belong to that thread's context. If the work needs Sahan's private account, route that part into an owner-authorized private conversation/run, using existing capabilities where possible. Obtain missing authorization through his DM or secure handoff. Private observations never enter the shared conversation automatically. Sahan receives the result privately and may approve selected content for publication back into the thread. Nishank can continue the shared discussion without gaining authority over Sahan's account. ## Required behavior 1. **Perform general browser and file tasks.** Accept natural-language goals across different, unfamiliar websites. Discover and upload an intended existing file; support download, inspection/transformation, and upload when requested. Site-specific scripts are not evidence of general capability. 2. **Collect, reuse, and revoke access.** Support secure input or login handoff for passwords, API keys, OAuth/browser access, and card details when needed. Keep secrets out of chat and model inputs. Reuse encrypted saved access and browser sessions across tasks and fresh browser runs. Owners can remove access; affected active work and saved sessions must not silently retain the revoked authority. 3. **Preserve private and shared boundaries.** DMs, personal memory, credentials, browser state, and private files stay owner-scoped. Channel discussions and intentionally shared material stay audience-scoped. Concurrent users cannot take over each other's sessions, account access, private history, approvals, or artifacts. 4. **Work in the background and recover.** Acknowledge requests promptly, provide useful brief progress, clarify material details, and offer private human handoff when needed. Persist the task through expired access, failures, and restarts; resume without blindly replaying completed consequential actions. Support cancellation and bounded execution. 5. **Confirm and verify.** Obtain owner confirmation for concrete consequential actions such as purchases, external messages, publication, or deletion. Changed action details require fresh confirmation. Confirm the actual website state or artifact before reporting completion. Approval for an action and approval to share its private result are separate permissions. ### TOTP: existing capability, unresolved product choice Reuse Hermes's existing TOTP implementation if automatic generation is included. The user's preferred flow is to supply the current code through secure input or a private browser handoff, keeping the setup key with the user. The original assignment explicitly requires accepting a TOTP setup key once and generating subsequent codes. **Manual code entry alone does not satisfy that criterion.** Resolve whether to demonstrate native automatic TOTP with the user's agreement or obtain an accepted assignment exception before declaring v1 complete. Automatic generation as an opt-in was discussed as a possibility, not settled. This choice does not require implementing a new TOTP algorithm and does not block the initial Slack/browser/routing proof. ## Now: build in this order 1. **Configure the selected local browser worker.** Pin Hermes and its browser dependencies, prepare a worker VM image with local Chromium and the Browser Use driver, enable the existing browser/vault capabilities, and provide reproducible setup and secret-free environment examples. Verify the chosen profile, browser, and workspace persistence arrangement. 2. **Configure routing and the secure access handoff.** Map verified workspace and sender identities to private DM or shared channel context and the correct resources. Build the selected vault web app and Slack sign-in flow around existing Hermes components, with owner-bound access requests and durable task resumption. Verify a two-user example, including denial of another user's access link. 3. **Exercise the complete reviewer flow.** From Slack, request browser work, provide access securely, reuse it, complete the file workflow, handle a failure, and remove access. Check shared collaboration and private boundaries using the actual enabled tools. Record passes, failures, and untested behavior. 4. **Fix remaining demonstrated gaps.** Prefer configuration, then supported plugins/extensions, then small integration changes beyond the selected hosted access flow. Validate owner-bound resource selection and controlled result delivery instead of rebuilding passing upstream features. 5. **Validate the hosted experience and package the result.** Repeat the acceptance checks with the developer's laptop out of the execution path. Produce the repository, entry link, demo, and access-management note. Attribute Hermes and other reused components accurately. **Done when:** the required behavior works through the deployed reviewer experience, the four deliverables exist, and the release evidence passes. Code volume and the number of custom components are not completion criteria. Record unsupported or unresolved requirements explicitly; do not mark v1 complete while they remain unmet. ## Release evidence | Area | Evidence required | | --- | --- | | Inference authentication and funding | Verify the chosen ChatGPT/Codex OAuth route supports the owner's account and intended hosted reviewer use. Record observed model-usage accounting and any separate charges. Exercise authentication refresh and restart persistence without depending on the owner's laptop. If this route is unavailable, record the unmet setup choice and agree an alternative before relying on it. | | General browser and file work | Complete real tasks on at least two different websites using the selected local Chromium + Browser Use stack inside the worker VM. Record driver/browser versions and confirm execution uses the local browser. Verify destination state independently of the agent's completion message. Find and upload the intended existing file, and complete download/inspection or transformation/upload. Treat two websites as an initial proof, not universal coverage. | | Access lifecycle | A reviewer signs into the hosted vault with Slack, securely connects access, and removes it. Reject wrong-user/wrong-workspace, expired, replayed, or altered access requests. Show secrets bypass chat/model/queue/logs and arbitrary agent code cannot read the vault's decryption keys. Verify durable save and resumption across worker replacement, saved-credential reuse in a fresh browser, saved-session reuse separately, and revocation of further affected access. Resolve and verify the TOTP criterion above. | | Recovery and durability | Exercise expired access or a controlled failure, supply the required input, and resume the original task. Restart the runtime and retain the correct history and artifacts. Verify recovery does not duplicate a completed consequential action. | | Routing, privacy, and collaboration | Two reviewers contribute to a shared task and retain its authorized context after restart. Test simultaneous private work, forged owner/tenant references, cross-user files/history/memory/skills, another participant's follow-up, and copied controls. Check that routing, enabled tools, and persisted data uphold the boundary, including another tenant identity. Demonstrate an approved result shared to a channel while private source data remains protected. | | Approvals and honest completion | Another participant cannot approve the owner's private action; changed action details or sharing audiences cannot reuse an old approval. Record actual outcomes, human intervention, failures, relevant versions, and known limits. Distinguish configured, verified, unsupported, and untested capabilities. | ## Four deliverables | Deliverable | Completion criteria | | --- | --- | | Runnable repository | Pinned dependencies/upstream versions, configuration, setup instructions, secret-free environment examples, and exercised verification instructions. Include integration code only where needed. | | Deployed reviewer experience | Slack invitation/entry link and hosted execution available without the developer's laptop. Two reviewers can use it without local setup or their own model-provider account. | | Approximately two-minute yyoreel demo | A real request, secure access collection or handoff, and verified completion. Include reuse/recovery where practical; inspect the exported video for exposed secrets before sharing. | | Access-management and known-limits note | Explain the chosen routing/profile/session boundaries, storage, access collection/reuse/revocation, TOTP decision, recovery, and verified limits. Identify upstream functionality versus clanker changes and explicitly disclose deferred operator/provider privacy controls. | ## Later Self-service multi-tenant onboarding/provisioning, additional messaging interfaces, delegated account access, advanced cross-team memory/grants, and configurable approval-policy UX are outside v1. Basic shared channel context, private DMs, ordinary owner confirmations, and approved result sharing remain in v1. Operator-access and model-provider-access privacy controls, including broader auditing, retention, training-use, and data-lifecycle controls, are deferred to clanker v2 or later as requested. This does not defer credential secrecy, protection between users/tenants, or honest disclosure of the deployed system's limits. ## Next Configure the selected local Chromium + Browser Use worker with Hermes's existing access capabilities, then prove the two-user DM/channel routing behavior and first complete browser task through Slack. Verify persistence across worker replacement and use those results to determine the remaining integration work. Settle the remaining TOTP choice before final acceptance. Obtain the user's review before external submission or contacting the founders. # Clanker Slack gateway PRD **Current POC delivery — 4 October 2026:** run the existing Hermes Slack gateway and local browser tools on the owner's MacBook. Sahan and Nishank use channel mentions after their admission and routing are configured. The cloud worker/persistence design below is deferred for this POC; see [POC_SCOPE.md](POC_SCOPE.md) for the current local acceptance criteria. **Status: Draft for user review. No implementation or provisioning authorized by this document.** **Date:** 2026-10-04 **Product contract:** One shared Slack gateway routes authorized tasks to isolated Hermes runtimes. The user experience determines the integration; adapt Hermes where necessary. ## 1. Review decisions 1. **Initial transport and host:** retain Socket Mode in one persistent Python gateway container on Cloudflare, provisionally. HTTP Events API on Workers remains an alternative, not a requirement for dynamic worker dispatch. 2. **Worker integration:** prefer Hermes's existing asynchronous runs API behind a trusted worker wrapper. Adapt the shared gateway's dispatch lifecycle rather than assuming the stock Slack adapter can dispatch dynamically unchanged. Experimental relay remains an alternative if the runs API cannot support the required controls. 3. **Initial Slack surfaces:** 1:1 DMs and explicitly admitted channels/threads; channel tasks require a bot mention. Reject MPIMs, Slack Connect/external senders and unknown audiences in v1. Preserve threaded replies, progress, clarification, approval and cancellation; broad native command parity is not required. 4. **Capacity policy:** bounded configurable workers, fair queuing between contexts, one active run per profile, and sequential ordinary turns within a profile. Queue later turns; owner-authorized cancel/control messages can act on the current task. 5. **Provisioning:** Cloudflare is preferred, but paid capability, budget, instance suitability and persistence behavior must be confirmed before deployment. This draft does not approve spending. These are proposals for review. Existing `MOD_HERMES.md` proposes relay; this draft offers runs API as the initial candidate and does not silently amend that document. ## 2. Problem and intended experience The stock Slack listener and reply code can be useful, but Clanker requires a task to outlive the gateway's current agent invocation and any assigned worker. Receiving ten task events from ten different authorized users must create ten owner/context-scoped tasks. Capacity may run only some immediately; the remainder wait fairly. None share a private Hermes agent, profile mount, browser state or task authority. The gateway is one trusted service. Multiple replicas, maximum throughput discovery and load benchmarking are not v1 prerequisites. One service may include transport and trusted control components; it must not execute arbitrary agent code. ### Concrete journeys | Journey | Required user-visible behavior | | --- | --- | | Private browser task | User DMs a request, sees accepted/queued status, receives useful progress and a verified result in that DM. The assigned worker loads only their authorized context. | | Ten independent users | Ten DM requests become ten distinct tasks tied to the right owners. With a smaller pool, queued users retain their place and eventually receive their own results. | | Shared collaboration | Two admitted participants contribute to one channel thread. They share its authorized conversation context, without loading either participant's private account state. | | Private access during shared work | Shared work identifies a need for Alice's private account. The gateway obtains Alice's authorization privately and creates/links a private task. Private observations return to Alice; sharing selected content requires her exact approval. | | Human input and recovery | A task waits for clarification or a private access form. The worker can be released after a durable checkpoint. Valid input resumes the same task once, even if the prior worker was replaced. | ## 3. Responsibilities and boundaries | Component | Owns | Does not own | | --- | --- | --- | | Shared gateway | Slack connection, admission, authenticated identity, audience mapping, durable task acceptance, safe progress/replies, owner-bound controls | Browser execution, deciding capacity, decrypting vault secrets in chat, arbitrary agent code | | Scheduler/pool manager | Fair dispatch, profile lease, worker assignment, capacity bounds, clean-worker lifecycle, recovery coordination | Deriving human identity from model text, Slack publication authority | | Isolated worker | Hermes, Browser Use driver, local Chromium, scoped profile/files, run events and checkpoints | Broad Slack/cloud credentials, other profiles, independent destination selection | | Durable context store | Versioned authorized history/browser/files and checkpoints beyond worker lifetime | Treating object keys supplied by agents as access grants | | Trusted vault/access service | Slack OIDC, owner/task/site authorization, secure submission, protected storage, durable access-ready signal | Sending passwords/setup keys through Slack, model inputs or queues | The gateway submits an authorized task to the scheduler. The scheduler selects a worker and supplies a scoped assignment. The gateway never assumes an event maps to a permanently allocated user VM. Storage and vault implementation are separate component decisions; this PRD defines their contracts. ```mermaid flowchart LR Slack[Slack] <--> G[One trusted gateway] G --> T[Durable task and delivery records] T --> Q[Queue and scheduler] Q --> W[Assigned isolated worker
Hermes + Browser Use + Chromium] W <--> S[Authorized durable context] W --> R[Bound run events and results] R --> G G <--> V[Trusted access and approval flows] V --> T ``` ## 4. Identity and routing requirements **G1. Authenticated identity.** Derive installation/workspace and sender from the authenticated Slack transport. Socket Mode uses its authenticated connection; HTTP, if selected, verifies the signature against raw bytes and rejects stale requests. Reject unknown installations/workspaces and senders. Model prose, submitted profile names, display names and email addresses confer no authority. **G2. Context selection.** Map a 1:1 DM to an owner-private profile. Map a channel/thread to a profile belonging to its admitted audience, with a thread-specific conversation session. Distinct audiences must not share private memory or browser state. Include tenant identity in every mapping. Fail closed on missing routes; never use a privileged default profile. **G3. Audience admission.** Confirm the channel is admitted and distinguish 1:1 IM from multi-person DM before context selection. Reject unsupported surfaces with a fixed safe response where appropriate. Workspace membership alone does not grant private-channel or personal-context access. Revalidate the permitted destination before delivery; membership/authorization changes suspend affected work for reconciliation. **G4. Distinct authorities.** Track requester, resource owner and output audience separately. Another participant can contribute to shared work without controlling a linked private task, approving an account action, reading private results or cancelling another owner's private run. **G5. Worker confinement.** Mount/load exactly the assigned context and its permitted files/browser state. Agent execution receives neither gateway/platform administrator credentials nor arbitrary storage access. Profile configuration is useful routing machinery, not the security boundary; the prior cross-profile session-search finding remains a release constraint. ## 5. Trusted envelopes These are required semantics, not a frozen wire schema. Trusted components construct and validate identity and routing fields; worker output cannot change them. | Envelope | Required semantics | | --- | --- | | Accepted event | Schema version, authenticated installation/tenant/workspace, sender, surface classification, channel/thread/message IDs, transport event identity, semantic duplicate identity, received time and normalized intent/input or scoped attachment references | | Task | Stable task ID, event association, requester, owner when applicable, authorized context/profile and conversation session, fixed permitted destination/audience, task kind, state/version, parent/private-task association when relevant, checkpoint reference and approved access handles | | Assignment | Task ID, run/attempt ID, context ID, lease and fencing generation, worker identity, scoped state references/version, bounded execution policy and authenticated callback/control capability | | Worker event/result | Task/run/attempt IDs, assigned worker and fencing generation, monotonic event sequence, event kind, safe progress/result or scoped artifact/checkpoint references, verified outcome evidence and failure/uncertainty classification | | Approval/input | Opaque request ID, task/run association, intended owner, exact action or input purpose, immutable content/action digest, audience where sharing is requested, expiry and single-use decision state | Accept callbacks only from the assigned authenticated worker and current generation. Reject stale/wrong-task output. Treat worker event text as untrusted content and apply disclosure rules before Slack delivery. Do not place credentials, broad bearer tokens or secrets in task messages or logs. ## 6. Acceptance, deduplication and ordering **G6. Durable acceptance before success.** Persist the accepted event and task/dispatch intent before acknowledging a task event. If persistence fails, do not claim acceptance. Keep transport acknowledgement within Slack's three-second budget; worker startup and model calls occur later. Unsupported/no-op events may be acknowledged without creating tasks. **G7. Two levels of deduplication.** Repeated transport delivery resolves to the original acceptance record. Also merge Slack `message` and `app_mention` notifications for the same underlying message. Do not collapse an intentional edit or separate user message. Use transport-specific interaction/command identities and make control consumption idempotent. Deduplication must survive gateway restart; the stock in-memory TTL cache is insufficient. **G8. Recoverable dispatch.** Persist acceptance and an outbox/dispatch intent together or use an equivalent recoverable transition. Queue publication failure leaves a retryable accepted task. Queue redelivery does not launch another active attempt. A duplicate event receives success once its original durable acceptance is known. **G9. Profile serialization.** Scheduler leases permit one active run per profile, including shared profiles with multiple thread sessions. Preserve accepted turn order within that profile. Fairly service independent contexts under configured capacity; a busy user cannot monopolize all slots. Throughput ceilings and multi-gateway routing are deferred. ## 7. Progress, replies and controls **G10. Delivery association.** Every progress, clarification, artifact and completion belongs to a task/run and server-selected destination. Socket Mode is inbound transport; replies still use Slack APIs. Workers return events/results to the gateway rather than directly posting to Slack. **G11. Durable delivery.** Record delivery intent and outcome separately from execution. Retry rate-limited/transient Slack failures with bounded backoff and respect Slack retry guidance. Restarting the gateway must not launch the browser task merely because its reply was undelivered. Reconcile ambiguous sends where possible; retain unresolved delivery status rather than claiming exactly-once Slack publication. **G12. Useful status.** Show accepted/queued state, meaningful progress, waiting reason, completion, cancellation or actionable failure. Coalesce repetitive progress. Do not claim an account action succeeded from a generated answer alone; completion requires worker outcome evidence or an explicit uncertain result. **G13. Owner-bound approval.** Validate authenticated clicker against the durable approval owner and current task/run. Bind consequential execution approval to the exact action; changed details require a new request. Private-result sharing approval additionally binds exact content/artifacts and destination audience. Tool permission approval alone is not publication consent. Enforce expiry and single consumption; denied, foreign and replayed decisions cannot resume execution. **G14. Cancellation.** An authorized owner may cancel their private task; shared task controls follow an explicit requester/owner policy, proposed as task requester only for v1. Queued cancellation prevents dispatch. Running cancellation reaches the assigned run and revokes further execution authority. Report `cancelling` until stop is observed, and disclose any external action already performed or whose outcome is uncertain. Late callbacks cannot revive a cancelled task. ## 8. Human input, persistence and recovery **G15. Waiting input.** Persist request purpose, owner, task and expiry outside the worker. Clarification text can use its admitted Slack surface; account secrets use the separate secure access flow. An access-ready signal carries a safe handle, never a password. Atomically consume valid input and record readiness once. Reject mismatched/expired/replayed input; input arriving after cancellation does not resume work. **G16. Worker release.** A waiting worker may be released only after a durable task/checkpoint transition. Run and approval state held only in process memory cannot justify scale-down. Resuming on another worker re-establishes the pending intent from persisted state; do not assume an old in-memory approval resolver survives replacement. **G17. Context persistence.** At task start, load the authorized durable context version. Checkpoint history, browser state and files consistently at defined safe points and before clean release. Use lease/fencing validation for checkpoint publication. Close/flush SQLite and browser state, or use a supported consistent snapshot; copying live files is not established as safe. Never reuse a dirty private worker for another context without verified reset/replacement. **G18. Failure classification.** Track accepted, queued, preparing, running, waiting-for-input/approval, cancelling, completed, failed, cancelled and needs-reconciliation states, with durable transition versions. A worker outage makes the current attempt interrupted. Requeue only after reconciling its lease, checkpoint and possible external effects. Uncertain purchase/post/delete outcomes require verification or owner input, not blind replay. A stored browser session is not a restored live page or unfinished action. ## 9. Hermes reuse and modification boundary Source findings refer to Hermes 0.21.5, tag `v2026.9.24`, commit `f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f`. Paths are under `hermes/`; these findings do not establish a deployed pass. | Source-verified capability/gap | Intended treatment | | --- | --- | | Slack `connect()` starts Bolt Socket Mode; registered listeners cover messages, mentions, commands and actions (`plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py:1601,1771`). | Reuse listener/reply functionality where it fits. Keep it in a normal Python runtime. Adapt dispatch and trusted controls; transport need not change. | | Message builder derives sender/team/session source, with known MPIM and route pitfalls (Slack audit). | Reuse normalization selectively, enforce G1–G5 before hydration/dispatch. Do not trust stock private/shared classification unchanged. | | Simple proxy mode posts text/history to `/v1/chat/completions` and consumes text SSE (`gateway/run_turn.py:2744`). | It proves remote invocation exists, but does not implement dynamic pool assignment, task persistence or owner-bound controls. Do not declare the architecture solved by configuring it. | | Runs API supports asynchronous admission, status/events, approval, steer/stop and durable idempotency (`gateway/platforms/api_server_runs.py:186`). | Candidate worker boundary. Use per-context authenticated scopes, stable idempotency/session IDs and a trusted wrapper enforcing task/lease association. Verify available capabilities against the pinned worker. | | Run ownership is checked by authenticated API scope; exact approval request IDs are supported (`api_server_runs.py:977,1072`). | Map Slack identity/owner to task authority in the trusted gateway. API scope is not automatically a Slack owner. | | Stock Slack duplicate cache is process memory; approval buttons gate on bot admission (Slack audit; `gateway/platforms/helpers.py:20`). | Add durable deduplication and owner-bound approvals. Reuse display components only after control semantics are adapted. | | Experimental RelayAdapter exchanges normalized events/actions with an external connector. Referenced connector repository was not publicly resolvable. | Alternative extension seam if runs integration fails a required journey. No requirement to rewrite the complete connector or adopt relay before testing the smaller candidate. | The shared gateway needs an adapted task lifecycle: normalize/admit → persist task → scheduler dispatch → bound worker events → durable delivery. Stock adapter use unchanged is not sufficient for that lifecycle. The precise patch/plugin boundary follows focused source validation during implementation, after PRD approval. ## 10. Provisional Cloudflare mapping | Responsibility | Initial candidate | Caveat | | --- | --- | --- | | One persistent Slack transport | Cloudflare Container running adapted Python Slack gateway, Socket Mode | Paid capability and reliable persistent-connection lifecycle unverified; Slack transport reconnects must preserve durable task state. | | Trusted task/control APIs and access UI | Workers | Keep arbitrary Hermes/browser execution outside Workers. Access/vault internals are separate scope. | | Dispatch and coordination | Queues plus Durable Object scheduler/profile leases and durable structured records | Queue delivery is at least once; scheduling, ordering and fencing are application responsibilities. Choose an authoritative record store explicitly. | | Isolated task runtime | Assigned Cloudflare Container, subject to proving required execution isolation | Validate that the offered isolation meets the selected worker boundary; do not call every container a verified VM sandbox. | | Durable scoped profile/browser/files | R2 with versioned manifests/checkpoints, provisionally | Object storage is not a live POSIX/SQLite/browser-profile mount. Restore/checkpoint integration and crash consistency require proof. | **Rationale:** retaining Socket Mode preserves existing adapter behavior and avoids making an HTTP rewrite the first prerequisite. Dynamic authorized dispatch is the actual change. A persistent gateway is acceptable for v1. If container availability/cost or the reuse experiment defeats this approach, switch to HTTP ingress on Workers and retain the same task contracts. Slack HTTP ingress requires signature validation and three-second acknowledgement independently of backend startup. Costs include paid container running resources, Workers/Durable Objects, storage/queue usage and worker capacity. No cost total is asserted without account capability and workload checks. Do not provision a paid plan from approval of this document alone. ## 11. Minimal v1 acceptance All scenarios below are **pending**. Record pinned versions, real versus synthetic environment, observed task/context/run IDs, assertions, failure evidence and limitations. Reuse the evidence ledger in `VERIFICATION_STRATEGY.md`. | Check | Required evidence | Environment | | --- | --- | --- | | A1: Ten distinct owners | Ten authenticated input events produce ten distinct owner/context-scoped tasks; bounded pool dispatches fairly; each result maps correctly; no concurrent runs for one profile. This is a correctness scenario, not a throughput benchmark. | Synthetic transport/worker test initially; label it synthetic. Real two-user checks below remain required. | | A2: Real private/shared routing | Two real Slack users complete concurrent DMs and contribute in a shared thread. Verify histories/destinations and rejection of foreign tenant, unknown route and unsupported MPIM without private worker dispatch. | Real Slack for normal paths; synthetic identities for unavailable tenant/surface negatives. | | A3: Duplicate and restart acceptance | Replay a task envelope and message/mention pair; crash between acceptance/queue publish; restart gateway. One accepted task remains recoverably dispatchable without duplicate active execution. | Controlled failure injection with synthetic transport; real Slack delivery smoke. | | A4: Owner controls and sharing | B cannot approve/cancel A's private work. Owner's expired/replayed/changed-action decision is rejected. A privately reviews exact result content and explicitly approves its shared destination before publication. | Synthetic negative tests plus real two-user Slack interaction journey. | | A5: Access resume and worker replacement | Wait for secure input, checkpoint/release worker, save authorized dummy access, resume the original task once on a replacement worker with scoped history/browser/files. Late input cannot revive cancellation. | Real Slack/access UI and isolated browser workers, dummy account data. | | A6: Delivery and uncertain actions | Worker completion followed by Slack failure/restart retries delivery without rerunning the task. A lost external-action response enters reconciliation and does not automatically replay the action. Cancellation rejects late output. | Controlled failure injection; real Slack/browser confirmation where applicable. | | A7: Runtime boundary | Agent code cannot read another owner's profile/browser/files, broad Slack/cloud credentials or trusted vault keys. Retest the cross-profile recall reproduction within the chosen execution boundary. | Actual deployed worker runtime with dummy secrets and adversarial probes. | Passing mocked source tests or one owner's tool-free Slack inference does not satisfy these journeys. No maximum-load experiment, multiple gateway replicas or full public SaaS onboarding is required to accept v1. ## 12. Scope limits and implementation entry This PRD covers the gateway experience and integration boundaries. It does not select the model funding arrangement, implement the vault, settle manual versus automatic TOTP, define the full VM/provider isolation design, add billing/onboarding, or require deferred operator/provider privacy controls. Those decisions remain in their own component scope. After user review, first prove one accepted DM can be durably dispatched through the candidate worker API and returned to its original destination, including a denied foreign approval and one restart. Then extend to the remaining acceptance journeys. Patch Hermes or introduce custom connector code only for demonstrated contract gaps. **Current blocker:** implementation awaits user review; there is no blocker to reviewing this draft. Cloudflare paid capability, worker boundary/persistence proof and the final adapter/API seam are prerequisites to deployment, not prerequisites to drafting the contract. ## References - [V1 scope](V1_SCOPE.md), [verification strategy](VERIFICATION_STRATEGY.md), [existing Hermes change proposals](MOD_HERMES.md). - [Pinned baseline](verification/hermes/baseline.json), [Slack source audit and probes](verification/audit-slack-notes.md), [isolation audit](verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md). - [Pinned Slack adapter](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py), [pinned runs API](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/gateway/platforms/api_server_runs.py), [pinned relay contract](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/website/docs/developer-guide/relay-connector-contract.md). - [Slack Socket Mode](https://docs.slack.dev/apis/events-api/using-socket-mode/), [HTTP Events API](https://docs.slack.dev/apis/events-api/), [request verification](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/verifying-requests-from-slack/), [interactions](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/). - [Cloudflare Containers lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/concepts/architecture/), [Containers pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/), [Queues guarantees](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/reference/delivery-guarantees/), [Queues external consumers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/configuration/pull-consumers/).

# clanker v1 scope and build approach **Current POC delivery override — 4 October 2026:** use the owner's MacBook as the host, kept running in clamshell mode with Amphetamine. Sahan and Nishank join the existing Slack workspace and use channel mentions of `@clanker`. Cloud hosting, VM pools and laptop-independent availability are deferred for this POC. [POC_SCOPE.md](POC_SCOPE.md) records the local setup and remaining reviewer checks; the hosted design below remains the broader v1 roadmap. ## State **clanker v1 is a hosted Hermes-based Slack assistant for general browser tasks and access management. Reuse Hermes first; focus clanker-specific work on routing and authorization, and add code only for demonstrated gaps.** The repository contains this scope, a verification strategy and source review, plus a pinned stock Hermes local baseline and clanker Slack setup files. The local CLI starts, 47 targeted upstream routing/session tests pass, and real Slack owner commands work in a DM and the test channel; see [LOCAL_BASELINE.md](verification/LOCAL_BASELINE.md). The full Slack/browser E2E, deployed reviewer experience, and v1 acceptance remain open. Upstream documentation and synthetic tests establish narrower capabilities, not that our chosen deployment has passed its requirements. **Selected browser architecture:** each assigned worker VM runs Hermes and local Chromium, controlled through Hermes's existing Browser Use driver. This is the selected v1 design; the VM pool, browser workflow, and persistence across VM replacement still require implementation and verification. **Selected access interface:** a hosted clanker vault web app uses Sign in with Slack to collect and manage saved access. Reuse Hermes's vault implementation and UI/API components behind clanker's authenticated owner and task checks. This integration is selected, not implemented or verified. The assignment permits third-party components and prioritizes a smooth working experience over code volume. A successful v1 may consist mostly of configuration, deployment, integration fixes, and verification. There is no requirement to build a new agent harness, Slack connector, browser engine, vault, or TOTP algorithm. Slack is the v1 conversation interface, with the hosted vault web app for secure access collection and management. The user reported that Sahan approved Slack identity replacing the assignment's Google-only chatbot sign-in requirement. Sahan and Nishank enter through the demo workspace invitation/entry link and use clanker without local setup or their own model-provider accounts. Inference is owner-funded. The assignment's core is browser tasks and secure access management. Private DMs, shared channel context, and protection between reviewers are additional v1 behavior requested by the user. A general self-service SaaS platform is not a prerequisite. ### Preferred inference setup: owner's ChatGPT account Prefer using the owner's existing ChatGPT subscription through Hermes's ChatGPT/Codex OAuth provider for the cloud baseline, to avoid purchasing separate API credits for eligible model usage. Reviewers still use Slack without their own model-provider accounts. This is the preferred setup to evaluate, not a verified funding arrangement. [Hermes documents](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers) device-code authorization, which lets the owner approve login in their browser while Hermes runs and stores its authentication on the cloud host. [OpenAI documents](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001542-using-your-chatgpt-plan-in-other-apps-and-sites) eligible plan usage in supported integrations; Hermes's exact account eligibility and quota accounting remain unverified for this deployment. Before relying on this route, establish that the intended owner-funded reviewer usage is supported, run a small inference request, and inspect the resulting usage and billing. Verify authentication refresh and persistence across a cloud restart with the owner's laptop out of the execution path. Subscription-funded inference does not establish coverage for hosting or separately billed browser/tool services. Record those costs separately. Any alternative paid inference setup remains a separate decision if the preferred route cannot meet the requirements. ## Reuse from Hermes Pin the Hermes version and required integrations, configure them, and verify their behavior in the deployed Slack experience. | Capability | Starting point | What clanker must establish | | --- | --- | --- | | Agent harness | Hermes's agent loop, tools, skills, and session machinery | General tasks work with the selected model and enabled tools. | | Slack interface | Hermes's existing Slack adapter and gateway | App configuration, authenticated admission, correct conversation routing, and replies. | | Browser automation | Local Chromium inside the assigned worker VM, controlled by Hermes's existing Browser Use driver (`browser_exec`) | Background browser work, uploads/downloads, secure login/handoff, scoped browser persistence, and saved-access reuse across worker replacement. | | Credentials and 2FA | Hermes's credential vault, Desktop vault form/API components, protected browser filling, TOTP support, and access-management controls | The hosted clanker vault web app authenticates with Slack and enforces owner/task/site access before saving or using credentials. Reviewers can securely provide, reuse, and remove access. Resolve the TOTP choice below. | | Profiles and conversations | Existing profile routing, DM/channel/thread sessions, memory, and persistence | The selected configuration enforces the intended tenant, owner, and audience boundaries across turns and restarts. | Start from the documented [browser integration](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/browser/), [credential vault](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/credential-vault/), [profile routing](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/multi-profile-gateways/#routing-shared-bot-chats-to-profiles-profile_routes), and [session behavior](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/sessions/#shared-vs-isolated-group-sessions). Native vault UI/API components cover CLI/Desktop use; the selected hosted web app adds the Slack identity and access-request authorization boundary. The complete collection, reuse, and revocation flow still needs validation. ## Architecture and routing contract **Use a shared Slack gateway and a pool of isolated Hermes worker VMs.** The gateway binds authenticated tenant, sender, and conversation audience to an authorized profile before queueing the task. The scheduler assigns a ready VM to that private or shared context; the VM pool manager maintains clean warm spares, adds capacity within limits, and removes excess idle capacity. Each worker runs Hermes, its Browser Use driver, and local Chromium inside the same VM. Profiles and permitted browser/file state persist beyond the worker's lifetime. The hosting provider, pool sizes, idle timeout, and storage implementation remain open choices. ```mermaid flowchart TD Slack["Slack workspaces
Private DMs and shared channels/threads"] <--> Gateway["Hermes Slack gateway"] Gateway --> Routing["Authenticated tenant, sender, and audience
Bind authorized profile and task"] Routing --> Queue["Durable task queue + scheduler
Fair dispatch, leases, bounded retries"] Queue -->|Assign task| Worker["Assigned worker VM
Hermes + Browser Use driver + local Chromium
One authorized private or shared context"] Queue -->|Pending demand| Pool["VM pool manager / autoscaler
Ready-spare target, VM limits, idle timeout"] Pool -->|Lifecycle calls| Provider["VM provider API"] Provider -->|Provision or stop| Worker Worker -->|Capacity and health| Pool Worker <--> Access["Enforced resource access
Only the current context's authorized state"] Access <--> State["Durable profile home, browser state, and files
Separate task and delivery records"] Gateway -->|Private access link| VaultUI["Hosted clanker vault web app"] VaultUI <--> Auth["Sign in with Slack
OIDC identity + server session"] Auth -->|Verified workspace and user| Trusted["Trusted credential handler
Owner, task, site, and action checks"] VaultUI -->|Secure credential submission| Trusted Trusted <--> Vault["Protected durable Hermes vault
Keys inaccessible to agent code"] Access -->|Authorized credential operation| Trusted Trusted -->|Resume after durable save| Queue Worker -->|Persist result| Delivery["Result delivery + owner-bound approval enforcement"] Delivery --> Gateway ``` These boxes describe responsibilities, not mandatory separate services. Reuse Hermes's Slack adapter, agent runtime, browser driver, vault, and session machinery. Routing checks may use existing configuration, supported extension points, or a small clanker integration. The scheduler and VM pool manager can share a backend service. The remote worker-to-gateway handoff must bind and durably record results before releasing a worker; reuse existing Slack delivery where it fits. Run Hermes in its upstream runtime; TypeScript remains the preference for clanker-owned integration code where appropriate. ### Selected browser stack: local Chromium + Browser Use Use the existing [Browser Use driver](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/browser/#browser-use-mode-default) with local Chromium. Hermes remains the agent making decisions; Browser Use supplies browser control through `browser_exec`. A hosted browser service is not part of the selected v1 baseline. Make local selection explicit instead of relying on credential autodetection: ```yaml browser: cloud_provider: local backend: browser-use ``` Build the worker image with pinned, compatible versions of Hermes, the Browser Use CLI, `agent-browser`, Chromium, and the required Linux dependencies. The pinned Hermes release installs/discovers the Browser Use CLI separately; pinning Hermes alone does not pin that driver. Complete installation during image construction so assigned tasks do not depend on first-use downloads. Keep **Hermes itself, the Python executed by `browser_exec`, and Chromium inside the assigned VM**. Running only the browser there would leave driver code executing on the shared host. Expose only the current context's authorized profile, browser state, and files; a shared channel worker must not receive a participant's private account state. Persist the authorized profile state, including `state.db` conversation and tool history, plus the dedicated browser profile and required workspace files/artifacts. Keep the protected vault and its decryption keys outside agent-accessible profile mounts, as specified below. Clanker's task record references the Hermes profile and session rather than duplicating chat history. Default local Chromium sessions are temporary, so configure and verify a persistent browser profile; a dedicated local Chromium instance connected through CDP is an existing integration option. The exact persistence mechanism remains to be validated. Restoring conversation history and cookies does not by itself restore a live page, unfinished form, or in-flight action. Before accepting this stack, exercise secure credential filling and human login/handoff, saved-login reuse in a fresh browser, saved-session reuse separately, download/inspection or transformation/upload, owner/audience separation, revocation, and recovery after worker replacement. These are pending acceptance checks, not capabilities already verified in clanker's local baseline. ### Selected access flow: hosted vault + Sign in with Slack Send the owner a private link to an expiring access request. The hosted clanker vault web app authenticates with Slack OpenID Connect and can reuse a valid server session for later visits. Validate the token signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and nonce, and validate OAuth state on the redirect. Match the verified Slack `team_id` and `user_id` to the request's tenant and owner; the server also binds the task, site origin, and permitted action. Reject a mismatched identity, expired request, or replay, and consume the request once on successful submission. Neither an email address, URL parameter, nor possession of the link grants access. This Sign in with Slack flow is separate from the Slack bot installation OAuth flow. Reuse Hermes's vault storage, validation, browser-fill/TOTP primitives, and existing Desktop form/API components where suitable. Clanker supplies the hosted page, authenticated session, request authorization, and task-resumption integration; exposing the general Hermes dashboard or accepting a client-selected profile is not that boundary. The existing optional setup-key field is reusable capability, not a decision to enable automatic TOTP; the product choice below remains unresolved. Submit secrets directly from the secure form to a trusted credential handler. Passwords and setup keys must bypass Slack, model inputs, task queue payloads, and application logs. The handler selects authorized storage from trusted identity, persists it durably, and returns only a handle and safe metadata. Keep the handler and decryption keys in an execution boundary inaccessible to arbitrary agent code; a context-local profile switch or a vault key beside agent-readable files does not enforce this. Authorized browser filling uses the protected path without returning the secret to the model. The exact boundary and Hermes integration require implementation and verification. Persist `waiting_for_input` and the access request independently of the worker VM. After a successful durable save, atomically consume the request and record the task's readiness for resumption, with idempotent dispatch so retries cannot lose or duplicate the resume transition. Requeue the original task with the credential handle, not the secret; an active worker need not remain online while the owner fills the form. Verify that saving during worker replacement resumes the correct task and that removing access prevents further affected credential use and saved-session reuse. | Routing decision | Required behavior | | --- | --- | | Tenant | Derive workspace/installation identity from authenticated Slack events. Include it in user, conversation, and resource routing. Reject unknown or unauthorized requesters instead of falling into a privileged default. | | Conversation and audience | A 1:1 DM loads that user's private context. A channel/thread loads context authorized for that channel's audience. Workspace membership alone does not reveal private-channel history. | | Requester and resource owner | Keep the sender, account/resource owner, and conversation audience distinct. Validate ownership before using credentials, browsers, files, history, or controls. Another participant's follow-up conveys no authority over someone else's private work. | | Context and tools | Scope memory, session recall, learned skills, files, artifacts, browser state, and credentials to the current authorized context. Prompt instructions and model-supplied owner IDs cannot grant access. | | Result destination | Return private account results privately. Sharing requires the owner's approval of the specific content and audience. Shared output grants no access to its source account or private files. | Session separation and profile routing are useful controls, but must be tested together with tools and persistence. Shared-profile memory or session recall must not expose DM content in a channel. Model-generated code must not have unrestricted access to other owners' files, the shared history store, or platform administrator credentials. Use supported scoped tools and isolated execution where needed; disable or adapt a tool whose access cannot be constrained. Keep retained history, recovery state, browser access, and artifacts durable across restarts, with their owner/audience associations intact. Use existing persistence when it meets these needs. The VM execution boundary and local browser stack above are selected; the cloud vendor, storage technology, and exact profile/session mapping remain implementation choices. For v1 delivery, the reviewers use one demo workspace. Routing must still carry tenant identity and be checked against another tenant identity without requiring a public onboarding or provisioning product. ### Example: collaboration involving a private account Sahan and Nishank discuss a report in a shared thread. Both contributions belong to that thread's context. If the work needs Sahan's private account, route that part into an owner-authorized private conversation/run, using existing capabilities where possible. Obtain missing authorization through his DM or secure handoff. Private observations never enter the shared conversation automatically. Sahan receives the result privately and may approve selected content for publication back into the thread. Nishank can continue the shared discussion without gaining authority over Sahan's account. ## Required behavior 1. **Perform general browser and file tasks.** Accept natural-language goals across different, unfamiliar websites. Discover and upload an intended existing file; support download, inspection/transformation, and upload when requested. Site-specific scripts are not evidence of general capability. 2. **Collect, reuse, and revoke access.** Support secure input or login handoff for passwords, API keys, OAuth/browser access, and card details when needed. Keep secrets out of chat and model inputs. Reuse encrypted saved access and browser sessions across tasks and fresh browser runs. Owners can remove access; affected active work and saved sessions must not silently retain the revoked authority. 3. **Preserve private and shared boundaries.** DMs, personal memory, credentials, browser state, and private files stay owner-scoped. Channel discussions and intentionally shared material stay audience-scoped. Concurrent users cannot take over each other's sessions, account access, private history, approvals, or artifacts. 4. **Work in the background and recover.** Acknowledge requests promptly, provide useful brief progress, clarify material details, and offer private human handoff when needed. Persist the task through expired access, failures, and restarts; resume without blindly replaying completed consequential actions. Support cancellation and bounded execution. 5. **Confirm and verify.** Obtain owner confirmation for concrete consequential actions such as purchases, external messages, publication, or deletion. Changed action details require fresh confirmation. Confirm the actual website state or artifact before reporting completion. Approval for an action and approval to share its private result are separate permissions. ### TOTP: existing capability, unresolved product choice Reuse Hermes's existing TOTP implementation if automatic generation is included. The user's preferred flow is to supply the current code through secure input or a private browser handoff, keeping the setup key with the user. The original assignment explicitly requires accepting a TOTP setup key once and generating subsequent codes. **Manual code entry alone does not satisfy that criterion.** Resolve whether to demonstrate native automatic TOTP with the user's agreement or obtain an accepted assignment exception before declaring v1 complete.
