# Hermes persistence prototype and restart contract

Status: **local dummy-data prototype; cloud transport and runtime lifecycle are not implemented**. Reviewed 2026-10-04. No real credentials or browser profiles were read, exported, restored, or uploaded. The pinned Hermes checkout is unchanged; this utility does not replace its agent loop, tools, browser driver, or gateway.

## What is executable now

Run the independent dummy-data tests from the repository root:

```sh
.local/hermes-lab/venv/bin/python -B deployment/cloudflare/persistence/test_snapshot_fixture.py
```

`snapshot_fixture.py` provides offline `export` and `restore` commands. Inspect their help before using them. Exports require an explicit include list, `--quiescent`, `--allow-dummy-private-data`, and a source marker named `.clanker-dummy-fixture` whose exact content is `CLANKER DUMMY DATA ONLY\n`. **Do not put that marker in a real Hermes home.** Tests create and remove all dummy homes under a temporary directory.

The include list is relative to exactly one private home. A future live adapter must inventory all durable paths used by the selected upstream configuration; this fixture utility does not discover a complete Hermes backup set. The tests select `state.db`, `config.yaml`, fake `auth.json`, a file directory, and a fake browser-profile directory. No source home is inferred from environment variables.

Exports use SQLite's [online backup API](https://www.sqlite.org/backup.html), through Python's [`Connection.backup`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/sqlite3.html#sqlite3.Connection.backup), for files with a SQLite header. This includes committed WAL contents and produces a standalone database; copying only a live `.db` file is insufficient. Database-suffixed files with an invalid header are refused. Quiescence remains required because a database snapshot cannot make a collection of independent files/databases transactionally consistent.

Each successful bundle contains:

```text
<checkpoint-id>/
  home.tar       # uncompressed, regular-file-only, private data
  manifest.json  # version, owner, generation, archive checksum, per-file checksums
```

The returned receipt contains only `owner_id`, `generation`, `manifest_sha256`, and `file_count`. All file contents and path metadata are private; the manifest is not safe for public logs. Bundles are **not encrypted** by this prototype. Directories use mode 0700 and files 0600. Production storage needs its separately reviewed private/encrypted transport and key-access policy before real data can be used.

Restore requires the expected owner, exact generation, and manifest SHA-256 from a trusted controller record. Reading these values from the bundle itself would remove the ownership/integrity check. Hashes detect tampering only while that external reference remains trusted; they are not authentication by themselves. The utility rejects mismatches, corruption, missing/extra/duplicate members, symlinks, special files, unsafe paths, and existing destinations. It verifies into a private sibling staging directory before atomically renaming it. A local publish lock serializes cooperating publishers; it is not a distributed lease or an adversarial filesystem sandbox.

Every directory component created inside the private staging root is explicitly set to 0700 through directory file descriptors, including intermediate directories under a normal 022 umask. Publication uses the platform's atomic no-replace primitive: macOS `renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL)` or Linux `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)`. A competing destination is preserved even when its creator ignores the advisory lock. An unavailable primitive, unsupported platform, or unsupported filesystem causes explicit refusal, with no check-then-rename fallback. Source/destination parent directories must still be trusted and stable; this does not defend against a hostile process replacing ancestors. The native macOS path was exercised locally; the Linux path requires its own runtime check before deployment. References: [Apple rename manual](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/man/man2/rename.2), [Apple flag definitions](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/sys/stdio.h), [Linux rename manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/renameat2.2.html), [Linux flag definitions](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/include/uapi/linux/fs.h).

Limits are deliberately small for the fixture: 1,024 files/pending directory entries, 64 MiB aggregate payload, 1 MiB manifest, a bounded uncompressed archive, and a cooperative 20-second processing deadline. These limits are not a measured production browser-profile size. Slow filesystem calls are not subject to a hard preemptive wall-clock deadline. No compression, extraction shell command, cloud client, subprocess, or network call is used.

Excluded volatile entries: names `SingletonLock`, `SingletonCookie`, `SingletonSocket`, `DevToolsActivePort`, `LOCK`; suffixes `.pid`, `.sock`, `.socket`, `.lock`, `-wal`, `-shm`, `-journal`. Nonvolatile symlinks/special files fail export. This is an explicit fixture exclusion policy, not a complete inventory of all upstream runtime artifacts. The live inventory must review any legitimate durable file matching these patterns.

## Cloudflare persistence choices

| Choice | Supported primitive | Remaining integration / tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default scheduling + immutable R2 checkpoints | Normal ephemeral root filesystem; export SQLite through its backup API and copy quiescent files into immutable private objects | Supports the `basic` gateway sizing option. Needs export/upload/commit/restore hooks, lifecycle control, owner checks, credential checkpoint handling, and application-consistent checkpoints. Last completed checkpoint defines recovery, not the last local write. |
| `durable_object` scheduling + native filesystem snapshots | `snapshotContainer()` captures the writable root filesystem; store its handle in DO storage and restore on start | Public beta; direct Container API required, not the `Container` SDK class. No `basic`; snapshots are image-version-bound, expire after 30 days without restoration, and exclude memory/processes/separate mounts. Still needs quiescence, owner/grant fencing, checkpoint selection and recovery tests. |
| Live SQLite on an R2 FUSE mount | Object-storage access through FUSE | Not selected: Cloudflare explicitly says FUSE lacks full POSIX semantics. It is not evidence that Hermes SQLite WAL/locking or browser databases are safe on that mount. |

Sources: [Cloudflare filesystem lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/faq/#is-disk-persistent-what-happens-to-my-disk-when-my-container-sleeps), [snapshot behavior](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/guides/snapshots/), [API exclusions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/api/durable-object-container/#snapshotcontainer), [scheduling policy](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/configuration/scheduling-policy/), [R2 FUSE limitations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/examples/r2-fuse-mount/).

This prototype establishes a file-bundle format usable by an R2 adapter; it does not choose or implement either cloud option. Both require paid Containers. Native snapshots are not continuous durable storage, and their documented semantics do not prove application-consistent SQLite/browser recovery.

## Three-owner runtime boundary

The trusted Slack ingress resolves verified workspace/user identifiers to owner IDs. Up to three isolated full Hermes runtimes can be leased simultaneously. Each receives only its owner's home, browser state, workspace files, and authorized credentials. A shared Slack channel does not authorize access to another owner's checkpoint. Do not select checkpoints from prompt text, display names, arbitrary object keys, or caller-chosen container names.

A controller record must bind:

```json
{
  "owner_id": "controller-derived-owner-id",
  "checkpoint_id": "controller-generated-immutable-id",
  "generation": 7,
  "manifest_sha256": "trusted-completed-bundle-digest",
  "image_digest": "reviewed-pinned-runtime-image",
  "credential_grant_id": "opaque-owner-bound-grant-reference",
  "lease_epoch": 12,
  "lease_holder": "specific-runtime-instance",
  "status": "checkpointed"
}
```

This is a design record, not an implemented schema in the prototype. Native snapshots would store an opaque snapshot handle in place of the R2 bundle reference. The controller alone manages credentials needed to access all owners' storage; those broad credentials must never enter an agent runtime. A scoped storage operation must check the current owner/lease/generation outside the model before fetching private state.

## Planned release and restore protocol

1. **Fence work.** The controller holds one active lease for that owner's writable home and credential grant. Reject new turns; drain the active turn or cancel it into a durable interrupted state. Close Chromium and browser-driver processes and stop all other state writers, including background/delegated tasks and OAuth refresh. `--quiescent` only asserts this; the prototype does not inspect processes or establish the fence.
2. **Checkpoint privately.** Export the selected SQLite databases, private config/auth state, files and fully closed browser profile. Do not copy a live profile and assume cookies, LevelDB and other browser state are coherent. Save files outside the home's tree, never in the image. Keep model-provider and Slack administration credentials out of worker bundles unless that exact worker requires them.
3. **Publish before releasing.** For R2, upload the archive and manifest under a new immutable owner/checkpoint key; verify their lengths/hashes by reading through private R2 APIs. Commit the completed reference and lease epoch in one authoritative DO storage transaction. R2 object read-after-write is strongly consistent, but that does not make two object uploads and the DO record one transaction. An incomplete upload is an orphan, not the latest checkpoint. Use conditional creation where appropriate. Never publish through a cached/public bucket URL. [R2 consistency](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/reference/consistency/), [conditional object writes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/workers/workers-api-reference/).
4. **Release and later restore.** Release a worker only after the commit is acknowledged. Before a new start, verify the owner/grant mapping, acquire a fresh lease, confirm that the previous runtime cannot still act, and resolve exactly the trusted completed checkpoint. Verify/stage into an absent private home; only then start unmodified pinned Hermes. Bad/missing checkpoints enter `restore_failed`; do not silently start an empty home, another owner's home, or an older checkpoint. Startup config cannot re-adopt host/global logins.
5. **Reconcile interruption.** Unexpected process/host death may lose writes since the last completed checkpoint. Mark in-flight work `needs_reconciliation`; query the destination's state before repeating external actions. Neither a restored SQLite file nor a filesystem snapshot proves exactly-once effects. Preserve an independent durable intake/action record so replayed Slack events or a repeated restore do not automatically re-execute a mutation.

Cloudflare can stop an active container for host events; it sends SIGTERM, then allows up to 15 minutes before SIGKILL. Crash/OOM does not guarantee that a final export will run. Periodic/task-boundary checkpoints plus explicit recovery policy are required; no zero-data-loss guarantee is made. Stock gateway restart/session behavior does not supply the distributed dispatch/commit protocol above. [Platform lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/faq/#how-long-can-instances-run-for-what-happens-when-a-host-server-is-shut-down).

## OAuth grant duplication guard

Do not seed three homes with the owner's existing refresh grant. Persist the grant-to-owner relationship in the controller and permit at most one active refresh-capable runtime for a grant. A lease timeout by itself does not revoke tokens already held by a partitioned worker: fail closed until termination is confirmed or the provider grant is revoked. A replacement worker must not resume an old snapshot while the earlier runtime remains alive.

Refreshed `auth.json` written after a checkpoint can make that checkpoint's grant stale. Before planned release, close the provider client, include its final auth state in the completed checkpoint, and advance the controller's credential generation. After an unplanned crash, do not roll back credential state automatically. Enter `reauthorization_required` if freshness cannot be established. Continuous, atomic refresh-token persistence would need a supported provider hook/credential broker or equivalent separately reviewed integration; this prototype does not supply one. The controller record must live outside rollbackable runtime snapshots.

## Verification boundary

The local suite queries the restored database through SQLite, compares independent owner-specific contents, checks file and nested-directory permissions, confirms WAL-sidecar/lock exclusion, and rejects all six cross-owner permutations for three dummy owners. It also checks archive/manifest corruption, wrong generations, payload tampering, traversal/symlinks, missing members, source special files, limits, gates, and non-overwrite behavior. The export and restore race regressions create an empty destination immediately before the native publication call and assert that its inode and empty contents remain unchanged. Unsupported atomic publication is tested for explicit failure.

Still open before any hosted acceptance: real pinned Hermes state-path inventory; Chromium clean shutdown and restoration; OAuth refresh/crash handling; authenticated R2 transport; distributed lease fencing; DO commit idempotence; stale-instance termination; source image compatibility; graceful and abrupt restart; duplicate Slack events; destination-side replay checks; peak resource sizing. There is no deployed R2 bucket, container, or production encryption/key setup in this work.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline, dummy-data-only Hermes-home checkpoint prototype. No cloud client."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from contextlib import closing
import ctypes
import errno
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import re
import shutil
import sqlite3
import stat
import sys
import tarfile
import tempfile
import time

FIXTURE_MARKER = ".clanker-dummy-fixture"
FIXTURE_CONTENT = b"CLANKER DUMMY DATA ONLY\n"
MAX_FILES = 1024
MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES = 1024 * 1024
MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES = MAX_BYTES + MAX_FILES * 1024 + 10240
MAX_SECONDS = 20
SQLITE_HEADER = b"SQLite format 3\x00"
VOLATILE_NAMES = {"SingletonLock", "SingletonCookie", "SingletonSocket",
                  "DevToolsActivePort", "LOCK"}


class SnapshotError(ValueError):
    """Fail closed without publishing a partial checkpoint or restore."""


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise SnapshotError(message)


def canonical(value):
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode() + b"\n"


def digest(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def relative_path(value):
    require(isinstance(value, str) and value and "\\" not in value,
            "invalid relative path")
    path = PurePosixPath(value)
    require(bool(path.parts) and not path.is_absolute() and str(path) == value and
            all(part not in {".", ".."} for part in path.parts),
            "unsafe relative path")
    return path


def identity(owner_id, generation):
    require(isinstance(owner_id, str) and
            re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}", owner_id), "invalid owner id")
    require(type(generation) is int and generation > 0, "invalid generation")


def volatile(path):
    name = path.name
    return (name in VOLATILE_NAMES or
            name.endswith((".pid", ".sock", ".socket", ".lock", "-wal", "-shm", "-journal")))


class Budget:
    def __init__(self):
        self.deadline = time.monotonic() + MAX_SECONDS

    def check(self):
        require(time.monotonic() < self.deadline, "operation deadline exceeded")


def read_regular(path, limit):
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    with os.fdopen(fd, "rb") as stream:
        info = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
        require(stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) and info.st_size <= limit,
                "not a bounded regular file")
        result = stream.read(limit + 1)
        require(len(result) <= limit, "file grew past limit")
        return result


def hash_file(path, budget, limit=MAX_BYTES):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    size = 0
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    with os.fdopen(fd, "rb") as stream:
        info = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
        require(stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) and info.st_size <= limit,
                "not a bounded regular file")
        while chunk := stream.read(64 * 1024):
            budget.check()
            size += len(chunk)
            require(size <= limit, "file exceeds limit")
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest(), size


def fsync_file(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as stream:
        os.fsync(stream.fileno())


def fsync_directory(path):
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
    try:
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def atomic_rename_no_replace(stage, destination):
    """Use the OS's exclusive rename or refuse; never emulate with exists+rename."""
    require(sys.platform in {"darwin", "linux"},
            "atomic no-replace publication unsupported on this platform")
    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
    try:
        if sys.platform == "darwin":
            rename = libc.renamex_np
            rename.argtypes = [ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_uint]
            args = (os.fsencode(stage), os.fsencode(destination), 0x00000004)  # RENAME_EXCL
        else:
            rename = libc.renameat2
            rename.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_int,
                               ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_uint]
            args = (-100, os.fsencode(stage), -100, os.fsencode(destination), 1)  # AT_FDCWD, RENAME_NOREPLACE
    except AttributeError as exc:
        raise SnapshotError("atomic no-replace primitive unavailable") from exc
    rename.restype = ctypes.c_int
    if rename(*args) != 0:
        error = ctypes.get_errno()
        if error == errno.EEXIST:
            raise SnapshotError("destination already exists")
        if error in {errno.EINVAL, errno.ENOSYS, errno.ENOTSUP, errno.EOPNOTSUPP}:
            raise SnapshotError("atomic no-replace publication unsupported by filesystem/runtime")
        raise OSError(error, os.strerror(error))


def publish_new_directory(stage, destination):
    # Cooperating local publishers serialize; the cloud controller still needs a lease.
    lock = destination.parent / ".clanker-checkpoint-publish.lock"
    fd = os.open(lock, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        atomic_rename_no_replace(stage, destination)
        fsync_directory(destination.parent)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def private_mkdir(path, *, root):
    """Create/chmod every component within an already-private staging root."""
    parts = path.relative_to(root).parts
    require(".." not in parts, "directory escapes staging root")
    fd = os.open(root, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    try:
        os.fchmod(fd, 0o700)
        for part in parts:
            try:
                os.mkdir(part, mode=0o700, dir_fd=fd)
            except FileExistsError:
                pass
            child = os.open(part, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=fd)
            os.close(fd)
            fd = child
            os.fchmod(fd, 0o700)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def backup_database(source, target, budget):
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(source.as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True,
                                 timeout=0.1)) as src:
        page_count = src.execute("PRAGMA page_count").fetchone()[0]
        page_size = src.execute("PRAGMA page_size").fetchone()[0]
        require(page_count * page_size <= MAX_BYTES, "database exceeds limit")
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(target)) as dst:
            src.backup(dst, pages=64, sleep=0.02,
                       progress=lambda _status, _remaining, _total: budget.check())
            dst.set_progress_handler(lambda: int(time.monotonic() >= budget.deadline), 1000)
            require(dst.execute("PRAGMA quick_check").fetchall() == [("ok",)],
                    "database backup failed quick_check")
            # Produce a standalone DB, not a DB needing copied WAL sidecars.
            dst.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE")
    os.chmod(target, 0o600)


def collect_files(home, includes, budget):
    result = {}
    for value in includes:
        relative_path(value)
        source = home / value
        for parent in [source, *source.parents]:
            if parent == home:
                break
            require(not parent.is_symlink(), "source symlink denied")
        require(source.exists(), "included path missing")
        candidates = [source]
        while candidates:
            budget.check()
            current = candidates.pop()
            if volatile(current):
                continue
            info = current.lstat()
            require(not stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode), "source symlink denied")
            if stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
                with os.scandir(current) as entries:
                    for entry in entries:
                        candidates.append(Path(entry.path))
                        require(len(candidates) + len(result) <= MAX_FILES,
                                "file/directory count limit exceeded")
            else:
                require(stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode), "source special file denied")
                name = current.relative_to(home).as_posix()
                relative_path(name)
                result[name] = current
                require(len(result) <= MAX_FILES, "file count limit exceeded")
    require(result, "empty selection")
    require(sum(p.stat().st_size for p in result.values()) <= MAX_BYTES,
            "source bytes exceed limit")
    return result


def export_fixture(home, destination, *, owner_id, generation, includes,
                   quiescent=False, allow_dummy_private_data=False):
    """Caller must stop all writers; the quiescent flag is an assertion, not detection."""
    identity(owner_id, generation)
    require(quiescent, "all writers and browser processes must be quiescent")
    require(allow_dummy_private_data, "private dummy-data acknowledgment required")
    home = Path(home).absolute()
    destination = Path(destination).absolute()
    require(not home.is_symlink(), "source home symlink denied")
    require(read_regular(home / FIXTURE_MARKER, 128) == FIXTURE_CONTENT,
            "only explicitly marked dummy fixtures are supported")
    require(home != destination and home not in destination.parents,
            "checkpoint must be outside source home")
    require(not os.path.lexists(destination), "destination already exists")
    budget = Budget()
    selected = collect_files(home, includes, budget)
    stage = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=".export-", dir=destination.parent))
    try:
        payload = stage / "payload"
        private_mkdir(payload, root=stage)
        records = []
        total = 0
        for name, source in sorted(selected.items()):
            budget.check()
            target = payload / name
            private_mkdir(target.parent, root=payload)
            fd = os.open(source, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK)
            with os.fdopen(fd, "rb") as stream:
                before = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
                require(stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode), "source not regular")
                header = stream.read(16)
                is_database = header == SQLITE_HEADER
                require(is_database or source.suffix not in {".db", ".sqlite", ".sqlite3"},
                        "database header invalid")
                if not is_database:
                    stream.seek(0)
                    with open(target, "xb") as out:
                        os.chmod(target, 0o600)
                        while chunk := stream.read(64 * 1024):
                            budget.check()
                            total += len(chunk)
                            require(total <= MAX_BYTES, "snapshot bytes exceed limit")
                            out.write(chunk)
                    after = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
                    require((before.st_size, before.st_mtime_ns) ==
                            (after.st_size, after.st_mtime_ns), "source changed during copy")
            if is_database:
                backup_database(source, target, budget)
            checksum, size = hash_file(target, budget)
            if is_database:
                total += size
            require(total <= MAX_BYTES, "snapshot bytes exceed limit")
            records.append({"path": name, "size": size, "sha256": checksum,
                            "kind": "sqlite-backup" if is_database else "file"})
        archive = stage / "home.tar"
        with tarfile.open(archive, "w", format=tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT) as tar:
            for record in records:
                budget.check()
                path = payload / record["path"]
                info = tarfile.TarInfo(record["path"])
                info.size = record["size"]
                info.mode = 0o600
                with open(path, "rb") as stream:
                    tar.addfile(info, stream)
        os.chmod(archive, 0o600)
        archive_hash, archive_size = hash_file(archive, budget, MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES)
        manifest = {"schema": 1, "fixture_only": True, "owner_id": owner_id,
                    "generation": generation, "all_content_private": True,
                    "writers_quiescent_asserted": True, "files": records,
                    "archive_sha256": archive_hash, "archive_size": archive_size}
        data = canonical(manifest)
        require(len(data) <= MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES, "manifest exceeds limit")
        manifest_path = stage / "manifest.json"
        manifest_path.write_bytes(data)
        os.chmod(manifest_path, 0o600)
        shutil.rmtree(payload)
        fsync_file(archive)
        fsync_file(manifest_path)
        fsync_directory(stage)
        publish_new_directory(stage, destination)
        return {"manifest_sha256": digest(data), "owner_id": owner_id,
                "generation": generation, "file_count": len(records)}
    finally:
        if stage.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(stage)


def restore_fixture(bundle, destination, *, expected_owner, expected_generation,
                    expected_manifest_sha256):
    identity(expected_owner, expected_generation)
    bundle, destination = Path(bundle).absolute(), Path(destination).absolute()
    require(not bundle.is_symlink(), "bundle symlink denied")
    require(not os.path.lexists(destination), "destination already exists")
    data = read_regular(bundle / "manifest.json", MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES)
    require(digest(data) == expected_manifest_sha256, "untrusted manifest digest")
    manifest = json.loads(data)
    require(manifest.get("schema") == 1 and manifest.get("fixture_only") is True,
            "unsupported manifest")
    require(manifest.get("owner_id") == expected_owner and
            manifest.get("generation") == expected_generation, "owner/generation mismatch")
    records = manifest.get("files")
    require(isinstance(records, list) and 0 < len(records) <= MAX_FILES,
            "invalid file count")
    expected = {}
    total = 0
    for record in records:
        name = str(relative_path(record["path"]))
        require(name not in expected and not volatile(PurePosixPath(name)),
                "duplicate or volatile manifest path")
        size = record["size"]
        require(type(size) is int and 0 <= size <= MAX_BYTES, "invalid file size")
        require(record["kind"] in {"file", "sqlite-backup"}, "invalid file kind")
        require(re.fullmatch(r"[a-f0-9]{64}", record["sha256"]), "invalid checksum")
        total += size
        require(total <= MAX_BYTES, "manifest bytes exceed limit")
        expected[name] = record
    budget = Budget()
    archive = bundle / "home.tar"
    require(not archive.is_symlink() and archive.is_file(), "archive not regular")
    require(archive.stat().st_size <= MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES, "archive exceeds limit")
    archive_hash, archive_size = hash_file(archive, budget, MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES)
    require(archive_hash == manifest.get("archive_sha256") and
            archive_size == manifest.get("archive_size"), "archive integrity mismatch")
    stage = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=".restore-", dir=destination.parent))
    try:
        seen = set()
        with os.fdopen(os.open(archive, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK), "rb") as stream, \
                tarfile.open(fileobj=stream, mode="r:") as tar:
            for member in tar:
                budget.check()
                name = str(relative_path(member.name))
                require(member.type == tarfile.REGTYPE and name in expected and
                        name not in seen and member.size == expected[name]["size"],
                        "unexpected, duplicate, linked, or invalid archive member")
                seen.add(name)
                require(len(seen) <= MAX_FILES, "archive file count exceeded")
                path = stage / name
                private_mkdir(path.parent, root=stage)
                with tar.extractfile(member) as src, open(path, "xb") as dst:
                    os.chmod(path, 0o600)
                    while chunk := src.read(64 * 1024):
                        budget.check()
                        dst.write(chunk)
                checksum, size = hash_file(path, budget)
                require(checksum == expected[name]["sha256"] and
                        size == expected[name]["size"], "payload integrity mismatch")
                if expected[name]["kind"] == "sqlite-backup":
                    with closing(sqlite3.connect(path.as_uri() + "?mode=ro",
                                                 uri=True)) as db:
                        db.set_progress_handler(lambda: int(time.monotonic() >= budget.deadline), 1000)
                        require(db.execute("PRAGMA quick_check").fetchall() == [("ok",)],
                                "restored database failed quick_check")
                fsync_file(path)
        require(seen == set(expected), "archive missing files")
        # Permit re-export of this restored fixture, never masquerade as a live home.
        marker = stage / FIXTURE_MARKER
        marker.write_bytes(FIXTURE_CONTENT)
        os.chmod(marker, 0o600)
        fsync_file(marker)
        for directory, _, _ in os.walk(stage, topdown=False):
            fsync_directory(directory)
        publish_new_directory(stage, destination)
        return {"owner_id": expected_owner, "generation": expected_generation,
                "file_count": len(seen)}
    finally:
        if stage.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(stage)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="operation", required=True)
    export = sub.add_parser("export", help="export an explicitly marked dummy home")
    export.add_argument("home", type=Path)
    export.add_argument("bundle", type=Path)
    export.add_argument("--owner", required=True)
    export.add_argument("--generation", required=True, type=int)
    export.add_argument("--include", action="append", required=True)
    export.add_argument("--quiescent", action="store_true", help="assert all writers/browser processes are stopped")
    export.add_argument("--allow-dummy-private-data", action="store_true")
    restore = sub.add_parser("restore", help="verify then restore into a new directory")
    restore.add_argument("bundle", type=Path)
    restore.add_argument("destination", type=Path)
    restore.add_argument("--owner", required=True)
    restore.add_argument("--generation", required=True, type=int)
    restore.add_argument("--manifest-sha256", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        if args.operation == "export":
            result = export_fixture(args.home, args.bundle, owner_id=args.owner,
                                    generation=args.generation, includes=args.include,
                                    quiescent=args.quiescent,
                                    allow_dummy_private_data=args.allow_dummy_private_data)
        else:
            result = restore_fixture(args.bundle, args.destination, expected_owner=args.owner,
                                     expected_generation=args.generation,
                                     expected_manifest_sha256=args.manifest_sha256)
        print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
    except (SnapshotError, OSError, sqlite3.Error, tarfile.TarError, KeyError,
            TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        parser.exit(2, f"Checkpoint refused ({type(exc).__name__}). No success recorded.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Cloudflare control-plane preparation

**Local candidate only, 2026-10-04. No deployment, billing change, runtime start, Slack send, or account credential is included.** The user's current scope is three people (Tanishq, Sahan, Nishank), independent simultaneous browser tasks, and free-only investigation. This folder does not select the eventual runtime topology or amend the gateway PRD.

## Implemented and deliberately blocked

- A narrow Worker health endpoint reports `preparation_only`, never runtime readiness.
- An operator-only admin surface reserves, lists, and cancels **unstarted** runtime assignments. One fixed coordinator Durable Object persists the registry before acknowledging a mutation. Concurrent allocation is serialized; configured capacity is 1–3, with a hard ceiling of 3.
- Owners come from a fixed alias set and a trusted workspace/member mapping. Public input cannot supply a workspace, Slack identity, DO name, storage key, image, command, URL, or environment. Opaque reservation IDs and increasing generations are server-generated.
- Admin use is disabled by default; allowlist is empty, the workspace is a placeholder, and no admin secret is supplied. No public Worker routes or preview URL are enabled in the template.
- Runtime start/stop/snapshot/restore, arbitrary exec/proxying, Slack intake, model access, browser control, scheduling/fairness, and Hermes remote dispatch are **not implemented**. Those paths return `501` after authentication. An assignment is not a running VM, a task, or a browser session.

This reservation lifecycle is independently useful preparation. It does not prove that three owners need three permanent VMs: assignments are created on demand, and no container exists in this template. The three-slot bound currently applies to reservation records; a later executor must consume the same authority to enforce the actual runtime bound.

## Files and local checks

The code has no third-party dependencies. Node 24 can execute the TypeScript source used by the tests. A locally installed TypeScript compiler checks the handwritten minimal runtime interfaces; these interfaces are **not** generated Cloudflare types and do not establish platform API compatibility.

From this directory:

```sh
node --test test/control-plane.test.mjs
tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json
```

No install, cloud CLI, live SDK, real credential file, or network request is needed. Test IDs and the test credential are synthetic. Tests instantiate the same Worker/DO classes against in-memory storage; the fake concurrency gate tests application sequencing, not Cloudflare's implementation. A reconstructed class reads saved fixture state, not a cloud restart.

Observed locally on 2026-10-04: **13 tests passed, 0 failed** with Node 24.19.0; TypeScript 5.9.3 `noEmit` check passed. No packages were installed. The first test run exposed an overstrict expectation about simultaneous request arrival order; the test now checks unique monotonic allocations without assuming authentication finishes in caller-array order.

Wrangler is not bundled or invoked. Before using a future installed version, inspect `wrangler --help` and the help for the intended command. Validate the schema, generate current Workers types, and perform a local runtime check before considering any deployment. The `exports` configuration follows current docs and must not be combined with legacy `migrations`.

## Admission and operator API

`GET /health` is inert liveness. Every other route requires HTTPS, `PREP_ADMIN_ENABLED=true`, a valid configured workspace/owner map, and a privately provisioned `CONTROL_ADMIN_SECRET` of at least 32 characters in `Authorization: Bearer …`. Browser-origin requests are denied. No cookies, CORS, credential defaults, or secrets in URLs are supported. Do not give this operator secret to models, browsers, workers, or Slack users.

| Route | JSON body | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /admin/reservations` | none | List preparation assignments |
| `POST /admin/reservations` | `{ "owner": "sahan" }` | Idempotently reserve one unstarted assignment for an admitted owner |
| `DELETE /admin/reservations` | `owner`, `reservationId`, `generation` from its current record | Cancel only the matching **unstarted** reservation |

The caller is a trusted operator, not an authenticated Slack person. This API does not authorize Sahan to control Tanishq's tasks. Future Slack admission must validate transport identity and independently bind requester, resource owner, and audience. Identity-map changes require reconciliation of existing records. Do not reinterpret cancellation as permission to destroy a running runtime.

## Container lifecycle and persistence contract to implement next

The template has **no `containers` block**. Current Cloudflare pricing lists no Containers usage on the Free plan, so a free Worker does not imply free browser hosting. Keep paid execution blocked under the present constraint. [Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/).

If later authorized, the snapshot-capable candidate is a new application with `scheduling_policy: "durable_object"`. That policy is immutable, uses direct `ctx.container` operations, and does **not** support `max_instances`: the authoritative coordinator must retain a slot for every starting/running/uncertain attempt. Do not add an ineffective `max_instances: 3` to that policy. `basic` is absent from its supported start instance names; measure whether a supported type fits three browser workloads. This is a policy-specific restriction, not a statement that all Cloudflare containers lack `basic`. [Scheduling policies](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/configuration/scheduling-policy/).

Required state transitions:

1. Authenticated admission → durable task and owner/context mapping → bounded assignment with generation/fencing authority.
2. Validate the owner's credential grant and expected checkpoint identity. Restore into a clean runtime using the trusted owner, generation, and manifest digest from the controller. Never accept those values or an R2 key from agent output. Coordinate with [the persistence preparation](../persistence/).
3. Start the pinned runtime and separately verify readiness. A process marked `running` is not an authenticated, initialized Hermes/browser service. Dispatch only after the owner binding and restored state are verified.
4. Renew a bounded task lease. An outbound Slack WebSocket is not a proof that its managing DO remains alive; explicitly implement the transport host's keepalive and reconnect policy. Direct API inactivity timeout must be reapplied after DO reconstruction, and monitoring must be reattached. Do not use unbounded keepalive under a free-only assumption. [Direct Container API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/api/durable-object-container/).
5. Before release, quiesce Hermes/browser writers, close or consistently back up SQLite, publish and verify the checkpoint, then stop. Retain uncertain assignments for reconciliation. A stale attempt cannot publish state or release a newer generation's slot. Do not reuse a dirty runtime across owners.

Native snapshots preserve filesystem state, not memory, open pages, or unfinished actions; mounted filesystems are outside the snapshot. Snapshots depend on image version, and handles have a 30-day TTL refreshed by restore. Store snapshot ownership, generation, image identity, and expiry metadata in trusted durable records. This is an alternative to the proposed versioned R2 bundle transport, not an implemented second backup path. [Snapshots](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/guides/snapshots/).

No guarantee of preserving permissions between Unix users inside one direct-policy container is assumed. Do not use a UID switch as the owner isolation boundary. [Direct API process-user limitations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/api/durable-object-container/#exec).

## Acceptance still required

| Stage | Evidence required |
| --- | --- |
| Local application checks | Default denial, strict body schema, no caller-selected runtime, three simultaneous distinct reservations, duplicate idempotency, cap, stale cancellation denial, storage failure and corrupt-state refusal |
| Platform preflight | Current Wrangler schema/types, account capability and free-only feasibility, actual DO storage/concurrency behavior, no unintended public route, operator secret provisioning procedure |
| Three-owner browser execution | Three simultaneous tasks, distinct browser/profile/private files, no cross-owner cookies or recall, scoped credential release, no broad Slack/cloud tokens inside agent execution |
| Persistence/recovery | Fresh-worker restore, image compatibility, deleted/expired checkpoint refusal, quiescent snapshot, interrupted task reconciliation, stale-generation fencing, retention/backups |
| Slack gateway | Authenticated workspace/sender/surface gate, deny unknown owner, durable ACK boundary, restart-safe deduplication, fixed reply audience, owner-bound approval/cancel, reconnect and delivery retry without duplicate execution |

None of the local reservation tests pass these platform, browser, persistence, or Slack acceptance rows. Shared gateway concurrency itself is already supported by pinned Hermes; the unresolved work is the execution boundary and its lifecycle, not creating a separate Slack connection for each person.

"""Independent dummy-state oracles; never opens an existing Hermes home."""
from contextlib import closing
import errno
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import socket
import sqlite3

import sys
import tarfile
import tempfile
import unittest
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

import snapshot_fixture as snapshots


class CheckpointTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="clanker-persistence-fixture-")
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.connections = []

    def tearDown(self):
        for db in self.connections:
            db.close()
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def home(self, owner="owner-a"):
        home = self.root / owner
        home.mkdir(mode=0o700)
        (home / snapshots.FIXTURE_MARKER).write_bytes(snapshots.FIXTURE_CONTENT)
        (home / "config.yaml").write_text("auth:\n  adopt_external_logins: false\n")
        (home / "auth.json").write_text(json.dumps({"fixture": True, "grant": f"DUMMY-{owner}"}))
        (home / "files").mkdir()
        (home / "files" / "result.txt").write_text(f"private result for {owner}\n")
        (home / "browser-profile").mkdir()
        (home / "browser-profile" / "Preferences").write_text('{"dummy_profile":true}')
        (home / "browser-profile" / "SingletonLock").symlink_to("nonexistent-process")
        (home / "gateway.pid").write_text("12345\n")
        (home / "gateway.lock").write_text("volatile\n")
        db = sqlite3.connect(home / "state.db")
        db.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        db.execute("PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0")
        db.execute("CREATE TABLE sessions (owner TEXT, content TEXT)")
        db.execute("INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (?, ?)", (owner, f"private chat for {owner}"))
        db.commit()
        self.connections.append(db)  # Keep committed data in WAL during export.
        return home

    def export(self, home, owner="owner-a", generation=1, **overrides):
        args = dict(owner_id=owner, generation=generation,
                    includes=["config.yaml", "auth.json", "state.db", "files", "browser-profile", "gateway.pid", "gateway.lock"],
                    quiescent=True, allow_dummy_private_data=True)
        args.update(overrides)
        bundle = self.root / f"{owner}-{generation}-checkpoint"
        receipt = snapshots.export_fixture(home, bundle, **args)
        return bundle, receipt

    def restore(self, bundle, receipt, target=None, **overrides):
        args = dict(expected_owner=receipt["owner_id"],
                    expected_generation=receipt["generation"],
                    expected_manifest_sha256=receipt["manifest_sha256"])
        args.update(overrides)
        target = target or self.root / "restored"
        snapshots.restore_fixture(bundle, target, **args)
        return target

    def rewrite_archive(self, bundle, receipt, members):
        """Exercise structure validation even when a controller trusts its digest."""
        with tarfile.open(bundle / "home.tar", "w", format=tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT) as archive:
            for info, data in members:
                archive.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data) if data is not None else None)
        manifest = json.loads((bundle / "manifest.json").read_bytes())
        data = (bundle / "home.tar").read_bytes()
        manifest["archive_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        manifest["archive_size"] = len(data)
        encoded = snapshots.canonical(manifest)
        (bundle / "manifest.json").write_bytes(encoded)
        receipt["manifest_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()

    def assert_refused_without_restore(self, bundle, receipt, **overrides):
        with self.assertRaises((snapshots.SnapshotError, OSError, tarfile.TarError)):
            self.restore(bundle, receipt, **overrides)
        self.assertFalse((self.root / "restored").exists())
        self.assertEqual(list(self.root.glob(".restore-*")), [])

    def test_wal_backup_restores_committed_query_config_private_files_and_permissions(self):
        home = self.home()
        self.assertGreater((home / "state.db-wal").stat().st_size, 0)
        bundle, receipt = self.export(home)
        restored = self.restore(bundle, receipt)
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(restored / "state.db")) as db:
            self.assertEqual(db.execute("SELECT owner, content FROM sessions").fetchall(),
                             [("owner-a", "private chat for owner-a")])
            self.assertEqual(db.execute("PRAGMA quick_check").fetchone(), ("ok",))
        self.assertEqual((restored / "config.yaml").read_bytes(), (home / "config.yaml").read_bytes())
        self.assertEqual((restored / "files/result.txt").read_text(), "private result for owner-a\n")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads((restored / "auth.json").read_text())["grant"], "DUMMY-owner-a")
        self.assertEqual((restored / "browser-profile/Preferences").read_text(), '{"dummy_profile":true}')
        self.assertEqual(restored.stat().st_mode & 0o777, 0o700)
        for name in ["config.yaml", "state.db", "auth.json", "files/result.txt"]:
            self.assertEqual((restored / name).stat().st_mode & 0o777, 0o600)
        for name in ["gateway.pid", "gateway.lock", "state.db-wal", "state.db-shm", "browser-profile/SingletonLock"]:
            self.assertFalse(os.path.lexists(restored / name))

    def test_three_owner_roundtrips_and_all_six_cross_owner_restore_denials(self):
        owners = ["owner-a", "owner-b", "owner-c"]
        for owner in owners:
            bundle, receipt = self.export(self.home(owner), owner=owner)
            target = self.restore(bundle, receipt, self.root / f"restored-{owner}")
            with closing(sqlite3.connect(target / "state.db")) as db:
                self.assertEqual(db.execute("SELECT owner FROM sessions").fetchall(), [(owner,)])
            for other in set(owners) - {owner}:
                self.assert_refused_without_restore(bundle, receipt, expected_owner=other)

    def test_wrong_generation_is_not_silently_restored(self):
        bundle, receipt = self.export(self.home(), generation=2)
        self.assert_refused_without_restore(bundle, receipt, expected_generation=1)

    def test_corrupted_archive_fails_closed(self):
        bundle, receipt = self.export(self.home())
        with open(bundle / "home.tar", "r+b") as stream:
            stream.seek(512)
            stream.write(b"CORRUPTED")
        self.assert_refused_without_restore(bundle, receipt)

    def test_modified_manifest_fails_closed(self):
        bundle, receipt = self.export(self.home())
        manifest = bundle / "manifest.json"
        manifest.write_bytes(manifest.read_bytes().replace(b"owner-a", b"owner-b"))
        self.assert_refused_without_restore(bundle, receipt)

    def test_wrong_payload_hash_fails_closed_after_valid_archive_hash(self):
        bundle, receipt = self.export(self.home())
        manifest = json.loads((bundle / "manifest.json").read_text())
        record = manifest["files"][0]
        info = tarfile.TarInfo(record["path"])
        info.size = record["size"]
        self.rewrite_archive(bundle, receipt, [(info, b"x" * info.size)])
        self.assert_refused_without_restore(bundle, receipt)

    def test_tar_symlink_and_traversal_fail_closed(self):
        bundle, receipt = self.export(self.home())
        for name, member_type in [("auth.json", tarfile.SYMTYPE), ("../escape", tarfile.REGTYPE)]:
            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
            info.type = member_type
            info.linkname = "../../outside"
            self.rewrite_archive(bundle, receipt, [(info, b"" if info.isreg() else None)])
            self.assert_refused_without_restore(bundle, receipt)
        self.assertFalse((self.root / "escape").exists())

    def test_empty_archive_missing_files_fails_closed(self):
        bundle, receipt = self.export(self.home())
        self.rewrite_archive(bundle, receipt, [])
        self.assert_refused_without_restore(bundle, receipt)

    def test_duplicate_archive_member_fails_closed(self):
        bundle, receipt = self.export(self.home())
        data = (self.root / "owner-a/auth.json").read_bytes()
        info = tarfile.TarInfo("auth.json")
        info.size = len(data)
        self.rewrite_archive(bundle, receipt, [(info, data), (info, data)])
        self.assert_refused_without_restore(bundle, receipt)

    def test_corrupt_source_database_never_publishes(self):
        home = self.home()
        (home / "bad.db").write_bytes(b"not a database")
        with self.assertRaises(snapshots.SnapshotError):
            self.export(home, includes=["config.yaml", "bad.db"])
        self.assertFalse((self.root / "owner-a-1-checkpoint").exists())
        self.assertEqual(list(self.root.glob(".export-*")), [])

    def test_source_symlink_and_nonvolatile_socket_are_denied(self):
        home = self.home()
        (home / "files/leak").symlink_to(self.root / "outside")
        with self.assertRaises(snapshots.SnapshotError):
            self.export(home)
        (home / "files/leak").unlink()
        with socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX) as sock:
            sock.bind(str(home / "files/ipc"))
            with self.assertRaises(snapshots.SnapshotError):
                self.export(home)
        self.assertEqual(list(self.root.glob(".export-*")), [])

    def test_requires_dummy_marker_quiescence_and_private_data_ack(self):
        home = self.home()
        for kwargs in [{"quiescent": False}, {"allow_dummy_private_data": False}]:
            with self.assertRaises(snapshots.SnapshotError):
                self.export(home, **kwargs)
        (home / snapshots.FIXTURE_MARKER).write_text("not a fixture")
        with self.assertRaises(snapshots.SnapshotError):
            self.export(home)

    def test_fifo_fixture_marker_is_refused_without_blocking(self):
        home = self.home()
        marker = home / snapshots.FIXTURE_MARKER
        marker.unlink()
        os.mkfifo(marker)
        with self.assertRaises(snapshots.SnapshotError):
            self.export(home)

    def test_byte_and_deadline_limits_fail_without_publishing(self):
        home = self.home()
        with patch.object(snapshots, "MAX_BYTES", 8):
            with self.assertRaises(snapshots.SnapshotError):
                self.export(home)
        with patch.object(snapshots, "MAX_SECONDS", -1):
            with self.assertRaises(snapshots.SnapshotError):
                self.export(home)
        self.assertFalse((self.root / "owner-a-1-checkpoint").exists())

    def test_existing_checkpoint_and_restore_are_never_overwritten(self):
        home = self.home()
        bundle, receipt = self.export(home)
        before = (bundle / "manifest.json").read_bytes()
        with self.assertRaises(snapshots.SnapshotError):
            self.export(home)
        self.assertEqual((bundle / "manifest.json").read_bytes(), before)
        target = self.restore(bundle, receipt)
        (target / "keep.txt").write_text("keep me")
        with self.assertRaises(snapshots.SnapshotError):
            self.restore(bundle, receipt, target)
        self.assertEqual((target / "keep.txt").read_text(), "keep me")

    def test_all_nested_restore_directories_are_private_with_umask_022(self):
        previous_umask = os.umask(0o022)
        try:
            home = self.home()
            nested = home / "files/deep/nested"
            nested.mkdir(parents=True)
            (nested / "result.txt").write_text("private nested fixture")
            bundle, receipt = self.export(home)
            restored = self.restore(bundle, receipt)
            for path in [restored, *restored.rglob("*")]:
                if path.is_dir():
                    self.assertEqual(path.stat().st_mode & 0o777, 0o700, str(path))
        finally:
            os.umask(previous_umask)

    def competing_directory_before_native_rename(self):
        native_rename = snapshots.atomic_rename_no_replace
        competition = {}

        def race(stage, destination):
            # Noncooperating creator ignores the advisory publish lock.
            destination.mkdir(mode=0o700)
            competition["path"] = destination
            competition["inode"] = destination.stat().st_ino
            native_rename(stage, destination)

        return race, competition

    def assert_competing_directory_unchanged(self, competition):
        self.assertEqual(competition["path"].stat().st_ino, competition["inode"])
        self.assertEqual(list(competition["path"].iterdir()), [])

    def test_export_cannot_replace_a_destination_created_at_publication(self):
        home = self.home()
        race, competition = self.competing_directory_before_native_rename()
        with patch.object(snapshots, "atomic_rename_no_replace", side_effect=race):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(snapshots.SnapshotError, "destination already exists"):
                self.export(home)
        self.assert_competing_directory_unchanged(competition)
        self.assertEqual(list(self.root.glob(".export-*")), [])

    def test_restore_cannot_replace_a_destination_created_at_publication(self):
        bundle, receipt = self.export(self.home())
        race, competition = self.competing_directory_before_native_rename()
        with patch.object(snapshots, "atomic_rename_no_replace", side_effect=race):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(snapshots.SnapshotError, "destination already exists"):
                self.restore(bundle, receipt)
        self.assert_competing_directory_unchanged(competition)
        self.assertEqual(list(self.root.glob(".restore-*")), [])

    def test_unavailable_no_replace_primitive_has_no_unsafe_fallback(self):
        stage = self.root / "stage"
        stage.mkdir()
        destination = self.root / "target"
        with patch.object(snapshots.sys, "platform", "unsupported"):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(snapshots.SnapshotError, "unsupported"):
                snapshots.atomic_rename_no_replace(stage, destination)
        with patch.object(snapshots.ctypes, "CDLL", return_value=object()):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(snapshots.SnapshotError, "unavailable"):
                snapshots.atomic_rename_no_replace(stage, destination)
        native = Mock(return_value=-1)
        fake_libc = SimpleNamespace(renamex_np=native, renameat2=native)
        with patch.object(snapshots.ctypes, "CDLL", return_value=fake_libc), \
                patch.object(snapshots.ctypes, "get_errno", return_value=errno.ENOTSUP):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(snapshots.SnapshotError, "unsupported"):
                snapshots.atomic_rename_no_replace(stage, destination)
        self.assertTrue(stage.is_dir())
        self.assertFalse(destination.exists())

    def test_cli_roundtrip_reports_only_receipts(self):
        home = self.home()
        script = str(Path(snapshots.__file__))
        bundle = self.root / "cli-checkpoint"
        result = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-B", script, "export", str(home), str(bundle),
             "--owner", "owner-a", "--generation", "3", "--include", "auth.json",
             "--include", "state.db", "--quiescent", "--allow-dummy-private-data"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30,
            env={"HOME": str(self.root), "PATH": os.defpath})
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        receipt = json.loads(result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(set(receipt), {"manifest_sha256", "owner_id", "generation", "file_count"})
        self.assertNotIn("DUMMY-owner-a", result.stdout + result.stderr)
        restored = self.root / "cli-restored"
        result = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-B", script, "restore", str(bundle), str(restored),
             "--owner", "owner-a", "--generation", "3",
             "--manifest-sha256", receipt["manifest_sha256"]],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30,
            env={"HOME": str(self.root), "PATH": os.defpath})
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.stdout)["generation"], 3)
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(restored / "state.db")) as db:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Invoke the project-versioned Hermes source with dedicated local state.
# The gateway is trusted; enabled generated-code tools use the Seatbelt provider.
set -euo pipefail
umask 077

project_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
lab_dir="$project_dir/.local/hermes-lab"
source_dir="$project_dir/hermes"

if [[ ! -x "$lab_dir/venv/bin/hermes" ]]; then
  echo "Install the pinned baseline first; see verification/LOCAL_BASELINE.md." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -f "$source_dir/pyproject.toml" ]]; then
  echo "Hermes source is missing; expected hermes/ at the project root." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ -e "$source_dir/.env" ]]; then
  echo "The Hermes source has a fallback .env; keep credentials only in the lab home." >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$lab_dir/home" "$lab_dir/workspace" "$lab_dir/gateway-locks" "$lab_dir/managed"
if [[ ! -f "$lab_dir/home/config.yaml" ]]; then
  cp "$project_dir/verification/hermes/config.yaml" "$lab_dir/home/config.yaml"
fi
if [[ ! -f "$lab_dir/home/.env" ]]; then
  touch "$lab_dir/home/.env"
fi
chmod 600 "$lab_dir/home/.env"
if [[ -f "$lab_dir/home/.clanker-execution/fleet.json" ]]; then
  if ! env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" \
      "$lab_dir/venv/bin/python" "$project_dir/runtime/seatbelt/recover.py" "$lab_dir/home"; then
    echo "Browser execution is unavailable; continuing with Slack chat." >&2
  fi
fi

cd "$lab_dir/workspace"
# Credentials must be deliberately configured in the lab home. Keep HOME
# unchanged for platform compatibility; do not inherit provider/session vars.
# Command smoke: skip startup model/tool warmup until inference is configured.
exec env -i \
  HOME="$HOME" \
  PATH="$lab_dir/venv/bin:$lab_dir/home/node/bin:$lab_dir/home/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" \
  TERM="${TERM:-xterm-256color}" \
  LANG="${LANG:-en_US.UTF-8}" \
  HERMES_HOME="$lab_dir/home" \
  PYTHONPATH="$project_dir/runtime" \
  HERMES_MANAGED_DIR="$lab_dir/managed" \
  HERMES_GATEWAY_LOCK_DIR="$lab_dir/gateway-locks" \
  HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1 \
  HERMES_STARTUP_WARMUP_TIMEOUT=0 \
  "$lab_dir/venv/bin/hermes" "$@"
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the clanker modifications only to the audited Hermes pin."""
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import subprocess

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
upstream = root / 'hermes'
pin = 'f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f'
patches = [root / 'patches/hermes/slack-workspace-membership.patch', root / 'patches/hermes/nat64-url-safety.patch', root / 'patches/hermes/slack-unfurl-admission-race.patch', root / 'patches/hermes/hosted-vault.patch']
baseline = json.loads((root / 'verification/hermes/baseline.json').read_text())
if baseline['commit'] != pin or hashlib.sha256((upstream / 'uv.lock').read_bytes()).hexdigest() != baseline['uv_lock_sha256']:
    raise SystemExit('Hermes pin differs; review/rebase the patch before applying.')
for patch in patches:
    check = subprocess.run(['git', 'apply', '--check', str(patch)], cwd=root, capture_output=True)
    if check.returncode == 0:
        subprocess.run(['git', 'apply', str(patch)], cwd=root, check=True)
    else:
        reverse = subprocess.run(['git', 'apply', '--reverse', '--check', str(patch)], cwd=root, capture_output=True)
        if reverse.returncode:
            raise SystemExit('Upstream has conflicting edits; refusing to overwrite them: ' + str(patch))
for source, destination in [
    (root / 'runtime/slack_workspace.py', upstream / 'gateway/slack_workspace.py'),
    (root / 'verification/probes/test_slack_workspace_membership.py', upstream / 'tests/gateway/test_slack_workspace_membership.py'),
]:
    if destination.exists() and destination.read_bytes() != source.read_bytes():
        raise SystemExit(f'{destination} differs; review it before replacing.')
    shutil.copy2(source, destination)
print('Clanker membership, browser and hosted-vault mods applied to the pinned Hermes checkout.')

POC_SCOPE.md:3:**Implementation checkpoint — 5 October 2026:** automatic workspace onboarding and private/shared routing are live. The real third member was provisioned before first contact and received one welcome within three seconds. Its DM and both channels passed ordinary browser tasks after enabling the verified Seatbelt-backed native tools across all five contexts. Fresh browser-ready join provisioning and failure recovery passed with native profiles and fixture Slack transport. [Join evidence](verification/evidence/2026-10-05-slack-onboarding-mod.md), [browser execution and limits](verification/evidence/2026-10-05-browser-execution.md).
POC_SCOPE.md:5:Current delivery decision: 4 October 2026. The MacBook is the POC host. Cloud hosting, Cloudflare billing, worker VM pools and laptop-independent availability are deferred for this POC.
POC_SCOPE.md:7:**Execution decision — 5 October 2026:** use macOS `sandbox-exec` for this local POC, with one common policy template parameterized for each private or shared execution context. Record its deprecation and macOS dependency as the local fallback's known limits; VM/container execution remains a future upgrade. The actual Browser Use executor, terminal and Chromium process tree are constrained; Chromium's inner sandbox is disabled while the outer Seatbelt boundary remains required. Metadata exposure and absent quotas remain known limits. [Decision, acceptance checks and assignment note](docs/decisions/2026-10-05-local-execution-boundary.md).
POC_SCOPE.md:9:## Intended experience
POC_SCOPE.md:13:**Member onboarding trigger:** joining the configured workspace must start onboarding automatically, using Slack's `team_join` event. A member's first DM or mention must not be required to start provisioning. Onboarding means registering the verified workspace/member identity, creating a fresh member profile and state, applying the configured tool permissions and model access, activating admission and conversation routing, and sending a welcome DM once the member can use clanker. Private DMs use the member's personal context; channel tasks use the configured shared audience context. Joining does not connect personal website accounts or copy another member's memory, browser sessions or credentials. See [the onboarding plan](verification/poc_single_gateway/ONBOARDING_PLAN.md) for the exact contract. This modification is deployed in the local gateway; pinned stock Hermes required the versioned membership mod.
POC_SCOPE.md:15:**Selected browser driver:** use Hermes's existing Browser Use integration on the MacBook, with `browser.cloud_provider: local` and `browser.backend: browser-use`. The Browser Use CLI runs the browser code; Hermes remains the agent. The pinned Hermes implementation offers `browser_exec` only with terminal access because the driver executes Python on the host. Installing the driver does not itself grant reviewer tool access, create profile routes or establish isolation.
POC_SCOPE.md:17:**Browser access is automatic:** Browser Use is part of the ordinary-member defaults applied during onboarding, including the required execution permissions, driver discovery and dedicated context state. New members request browser tasks in ordinary language; they never activate a plugin or edit tool settings. Mark a member ready only after their resolved Slack tool inventory exposes `browser_exec` and the driver is runnable. Apply the same defaults to eligible existing members and shared-channel execution contexts. The [browser-default contract](verification/poc_single_gateway/ONBOARDING_PLAN.md#browser-use-by-default) includes first-request and recovery acceptance checks.
POC_SCOPE.md:19:**Browser prepared:** the installed Chromium and Browser Use driver are wired into all five existing contexts and fresh onboarding. Direct private/shared/private browser checks passed after correcting a harness-daemon naming collision. [Preparation evidence](verification/evidence/2026-10-05-browser-readiness.md). Slack Browser Use activation and execution-boundary checks have since passed. The intended reviewer invitations and closed-lid acceptance remain pending.

HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:1:# Hermes verification review for clanker v1
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:5:**Yes. All six release-evidence areas in `V1_SCOPE.md` still require deployment verification.** The repository contains the scope, verification strategy and scaffolding, with no configured clanker baseline or acceptance results. This review establishes documented capabilities and targeted source findings. It does not record any runtime PASS or reproduced vulnerability.
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:9:## Research baseline
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:15:## 1. Routing, privacy and collaboration
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:23:**Specific source finding:** `session_search` exposes a model-selected `profile`. Its dispatch also accepts a profile embedded in a session reference, then opens the named profile's database. The inspected resolution/dispatch functions do not check the requester's ownership. An outer tool restriction could change the deployed result; the full gateway call graph was not audited. Test or constrain this path before enabling it for reviewers. [Database resolution](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/tools/session_search_tool.py#L434), [dispatch](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/tools/session_search_tool.py#L577), [model-visible schema and registration](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/tools/session_search_tool.py#L769)
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:29:**Still required:** two simultaneous private tasks plus shared collaboration; authenticated workspace/sender mapping; rejection of unknown users/tenants and unsafe default routes; direct forbidden reads through history, memory, skills, file, execution, browser and credential tools; correct private/shared state after restart. Check reviewer command permissions with `/whoami` and restrict administrative controls. Include access by delegated work when enabled.
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:31:## 2. Secure access collection, reuse, revocation and TOTP
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:35:**Secure Slack input remains a likely integration gap.** The save-login tool returns `prompt_unavailable` without a supported prompt callback. A targeted search found no vault prompt callback wiring in the inspected Slack adapter or gateway runner/run modules. This is not an exhaustive wiring audit or a runtime failure. Verify a supported secure handoff before designing additional services. [Callback implementation](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/4ed093cb6be8a2fadb39e770898f6989fc67201d/agent/vault_backends/unlock.py#L34), [save-login guard](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/4ed093cb6be8a2fadb39e770898f6989fc67201d/tools/browser_vault_tool.py#L291), [Slack adapter](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/4ed093cb6be8a2fadb39e770898f6989fc67201d/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py), [turn runner](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/4ed093cb6be8a2fadb39e770898f6989fc67201d/gateway/run_turn_runner.py)
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:37:**Vault deletion does not establish complete revocation.** The inspected removal function deletes the stored entry; its CLI/TUI callers do not invalidate browser cookies or stop active work. Other integration layers could add that behavior, so test the complete lifecycle. [Store removal](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/4ed093cb6be8a2fadb39e770898f6989fc67201d/agent/vault_store.py#L384), [CLI removal](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/4ed093cb6be8a2fadb39e770898f6989fc67201d/hermes_cli/vault.py#L176), [TUI removal](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/4ed093cb6be8a2fadb39e770898f6989fc67201d/tui_gateway/methods_vault.py#L175)
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:39:**Still required:** secure collection through the hosted reviewer experience; dummy-secret checks in chat/model inputs/logs; saved credentials in a fresh browser; separately, reuse of a signed-in browser session; removal during active work; loss of access from live and persisted sessions and subsequent runs; expired-login recovery. Define and exercise API-key and OAuth access separately from password filling.
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:41:**TOTP remains a product decision.** Upstream automatic generation exists. The scope requires either agreement to demonstrate it or an accepted assignment exception for manual codes. Documentation cannot settle that choice.
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:43:## 3. General browser and file work
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:51:**Still required:** select one backend, discover the intended existing file, upload it, then complete authenticated download → inspection/transformation → upload. Verify real destination state on two different websites through natural-language requests. Test cloud/local file transfer, concurrent owner separation and browser persistence with that same configuration.
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:53:## 4. Owner approvals and honest completion
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:57:**Specific source finding:** the inspected Slack approval handler checks whether a clicker is admitted, then resolves using `session_key` and choice. It does not compare that clicker to the original requester or pass the resolver's optional request ID. Without a request ID, the resolver chooses the oldest pending approval. This needs a focused test for another admitted user, an old card and changed action details. [Button construction](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py#L4836), [interactive admission](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py#L5321), [approval callback](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py#L5480), [resolver](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/tools/approval.py#L138)
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:59:**Still required:** owner-only authority, exact action details, fresh confirmation after changes, expiry/replay handling, and separate approval of exact shared content and audience. Keep private account actions and their controls in the owner's private run. Independently observe the resulting website/file state before declaring completion. These requirements may be met by configuration and constrained existing paths; a new gateway has not been justified.
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:61:## 5. Background work, recovery and durability
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:67:**Specific source finding:** Slack ingress deduplication uses `team_id:event_ts` in an in-memory cache, with adapter-to-adapter transfer in the same process. That cache alone cannot survive a whole-process restart. Other protections may exist; replay after restart remains a test, not a reproduced duplicate action. [Slack ingress dedupe](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py#L4368), [cache implementation](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/gateway/platforms/helpers.py#L20)
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:71:**Still required:** measure acknowledgement and useful progress; privately supply missing input; resume the original task; cancel all relevant work; enforce task/time bounds. Use a fake submission counter and restart before submission, after acceptance and before reply delivery. Require one intended action, correct owner/audience, durable artifacts and truthful handling of uncertain outcomes. Replay the same Slack event across restart.
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:75:## 6. Inference funding, hosting and delivery
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:81:**Still required:** confirm the intended funding arrangement; make a small inference request; observe usage and any charges; verify token refresh and restart persistence on the host. Record auxiliary/delegated model routing and separately billed tools/hosting. Auxiliary models normally inherit the main model unless overridden, so inspect the actual configuration. [Auxiliary model configuration](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/configuration#auxiliary-models)
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:87:## Verification order
HERMES_VERIFICATION_REVIEW.md:95:**Review outcome:** the docs support substantial Hermes reuse, and targeted source inspection identifies specific paths to test or constrain. All six clanker release-evidence areas remain **UNTESTED** in the intended deployment. No install, deployment, paid request, external post or runtime acceptance test was performed during this review.

verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:1:# Private and shared context: source audit
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:5:## Answer
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:7:**The privacy gap is real in the pinned stock Hermes configuration with unrestricted tools. It is no longer only an untested possibility.** A local dummy-data probe returned another profile's private transcript through the normal agent tool-invocation path, with the current profile and multiplex secret scope correctly bound. Separate conversation IDs and separate profile directories do not, by themselves, enforce clanker's owner/audience contract.
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:11:## Scope and evidence standard
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:19:## Findings at a glance
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:29:## 1. Slack routing is useful and configurable
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:48:## 2. One profile for all users fails the memory boundary
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:56:## 3. Cross-profile recall is reproduced through the agent invocation path
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:96:## 4. Account/browser authority follows profiles and backend semantics
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:108:## 5. Execution isolation and sharing need explicit enforcement
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:122:## What this establishes for the design
verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md:132:**Configuration-only remains a candidate for a restricted tool set.** Separate audience profiles, private Docker mounts, unrestricted recall disabled, no host Python browser path or shared authenticated CDP endpoint, inline skill shell off, and constrained outbound tools can remove the demonstrated paths. This audit does not prove that every such stock configuration fails. It also does not verify one that preserves every v1 feature. Automated private-to-shared publication still needs enforceable owner/content/audience mediation; a manual workflow must not silently replace required behavior.
